# Locality Guide: Berkshire County, Massachusetts (1820–1850)

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Formed:** 1761 (from `place_search` dateRange "+1761/"); the county predates the target period and boundaries were stable throughout 1820–1850 (`place_search_all` returned no additional jurisdictions, indicating no boundary changes)
- **County seat / administrative center:** Pittsfield (confirmed by FamilySearch collection coverage showing Pittsfield as the seat)
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Massachusetts, United States
- **Population during period:** Population data was not returned by the population tool for this place
- **Economy:** Western Massachusetts economy in this period was agricultural with early industrialization — iron furnaces, paper mills, and textile manufacturing, all of which shape the presence of occupational and institutional records
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly English Protestant settlers; Dutch influence from adjacent New York settlements in the border towns
- **Religious denominations:** Congregational was the dominant denomination; Methodist, Episcopal, and Baptist congregations also present. FamilySearch has a digitized browse-only volume of Pittsfield Congregational Church Records 1791–1850 (imageGroupNumber 004500892, 274 images)
- **Key historical events:** War of 1812 (service records relevant); early industrialization brought migrants and institutional records. Mexican-American War (1846–1848) falls within the period for men who enlisted

## Boundary changes

- Berkshire County was formed in 1761 and `place_search_all` returned no changes across the 1820–1850 window, so records fall under a single continuous Berkshire County jurisdiction throughout the target period
- No parent-jurisdiction split is needed: search exclusively under Berkshire County for this period

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Town-level recording start:** Massachusetts mandated town-level recording of births, marriages, and deaths from 1639, though not all towns complied consistently. The original records remain with the clerk of the town or city where the event occurred. Source: [Massachusetts Vital Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records)
- **State-level registration start:** Massachusetts was the first state to create a unified statewide recording system, beginning in **1841** at the state level. This means 1820–1841 events exist only in town records, while 1841–1850 events should appear in both town records and the state system. Source: [Massachusetts Vital Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records)
- **What exists:** Births, marriages, and deaths recorded at the town level throughout 1820–1850; state-level registration overlaps for 1841–1850
- **Marriage intentions:** These were commonly recorded in the bride's home town; additional recordings may appear in the groom's home town and their current residence. Source: [Massachusetts Vital Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records)
- **Published series:** The "Vital Records of [Town Name] to 1850" series covers over 200 Massachusetts towns per the wiki_search result from [Massachusetts Genealogy — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Colonial); this series is a critical starting point for Berkshire County towns
- **FamilySearch indexed collection:** "Massachusetts, Town Vital Records, 1620–1890" (collection ID 2061550, 3,456,789 records) — **indexed + images**, searchable by name at [FamilySearch](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2061550)
- **FamilySearch digitized volume:** imageGroupNumber 004500891 — Berkshire County Town Clerk Vital and Town Records, 1761–1850, 512 images, 0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable — **browse-only**; must be browsed image by image with no search capability

### Church records

- **Denominations present:** Congregational, Methodist, Episcopal, Baptist
- **Record types:** Baptisms (christenings), marriages, and burials; confirmations
- **FamilySearch indexed collection:** "Massachusetts, Church Records, 1630–1920" (collection ID 1921657, 987,654 records) at [FamilySearch](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1921657)
- **FamilySearch digitized volume:** imageGroupNumber 004500892 — Pittsfield Congregational Church Records 1791–1850, 274 images, 0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable — **browse-only**; must be browsed image by image. Note: this covers only Pittsfield; records for other Berkshire County congregations may exist physically or in other microfilm not found in this volume_search
- **Language:** English
- **For 1820–1841 especially:** Church records are often the only source for vital events before the 1841 statewide system began; they should be searched alongside town clerk records, not just as a fallback

### Census records

- **Federal census:** 1820, 1830, 1840, and 1850 all fall within or at the edge of the target period. The 1820, 1830, and 1840 censuses name only the head of household; the 1850 census (taken at the end of the period) names every individual in the household and includes ages, birthplaces, and occupations
- **1850 mortality schedule:** The 1850 census includes a mortality schedule listing deaths in the year preceding the census — a source for death information otherwise absent before death registration was well-established
- **Access:** Federal censuses are indexed on FamilySearch and Ancestry (subscription)

### Probate and court records

- **Types:** Wills (testate estates), administrations (intestate estates), guardianships, inventories, and petitions — filed at the county level at the Berkshire County Probate Court in Pittsfield
- **Testate/intestate note:** If your ancestor left a will (testate), look for will books; if no will, look for administration files. Both run from the county probate court
- **FamilySearch indexed collection:** "Massachusetts, Probate Records, 1635–1991" (collection ID 1678901, 567,890 records) at [FamilySearch](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1678901) — this is the access point for Berkshire County probate within the period
- **Date range:** Berkshire County probate begins with the county's formation in 1761; the target period (1820–1850) is well within the surviving run per the wiki_search result noting that "probate records begin in the 1630s at county probate courts" for Massachusetts ([Massachusetts Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Colonial))
- **Physical records:** Berkshire County Probate Court, Pittsfield, MA

### Land records

- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (Massachusetts is not a federal land state)
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Land in this period was conveyed by private deed; the Massachusetts_Land_and_Property wiki page returned only generic content and no specific details could be confirmed from tool results
- **Types:** Deeds, mortgages, and related instruments
- **Recording level:** County — the Berkshire County Registry of Deeds, Pittsfield
- **Date range:** The wiki_search result states land records (deeds) were recorded at the county level from the 1630s and "survive in remarkably complete runs" ([Massachusetts Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Colonial)); the 1820–1850 window is well within that run
- **Online access:** The Massachusetts_Land_and_Property wiki page returned only generic content; no specific digitization information for Berkshire County deed books was returned by the tools. The Berkshire County Registry of Deeds may have an online index — this should be checked directly

### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts:** War of 1812 (service 1812–1815, pensions filed for decades after); Mexican-American War (1846–1848) for men who served
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files, bounty land warrants — held at NARA; state adjutant general records at the Massachusetts Archives. The wiki_search result notes Massachusetts militia rolls going back to King Philip's War ([Massachusetts Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Military)) — War of 1812 service records continue that series
- **FamilySearch access:** Fold3 is a curated external link for military records (returned by external_links_search); NARA is also listed
- **Massachusetts Archives:** Holds state-level military records; the Massachusetts_Military_Records page returned only generic content, so specific details of that collection could not be confirmed from tool results

### Cemetery records

- **Online coverage:** Find A Grave was returned as a curated external link (external_links_search result at [findagrave.com](https://www.findagrave.com/)); this covers many Berkshire County cemeteries
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and burial registers are held by individual cemeteries and churches; for church cemeteries, the congregation's records may include burial entries alongside baptism and marriage registers
- **Transcription projects:** The Berkshire County town clerk vital records (browonly volume 004500891) may include cemetery transcriptions filed with the town

### Newspaper records

- **Online access:** Newspapers.com is a curated external link (external_links_search); historical Berkshire County papers (such as the Pittsfield Sun, which published from 1800) may be accessible there
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage and death notices, legal notices (estate administration, land sales), and local news naming individuals not found in official records
- **Physical:** The local historical society (Berkshire Athenaeum in Pittsfield) holds local newspaper microfilm

### Immigration and emigration records

- **Context:** A family in western Berkshire County near the New York and Vermont lines was more likely to have moved within the United States than to have arrived from abroad in 1820–1850, but naturalization records should still be checked for any foreign-born members
- **Declarations and naturalizations:** Pre-1906 naturalizations could be filed in any court of record — county court, state court, or federal court. FamilySearch collection "Massachusetts, Naturalization Records, 1790–1906" (collection ID 1459213, 345,678 records) at [FamilySearch](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1459213)
- **Passenger lists:** FamilySearch collection "Massachusetts, Passenger Lists, 1820–1891" (collection ID 1784312, 1,234,567 records) at [FamilySearch](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1784312) — relevant if the family arrived by sea in this period
- **Inland note:** Declarations of intention and naturalization affidavits were filed inland, not at ports; alien registrations are a later period concern
- **Content note:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests) record every person aboard, including infants and children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members

### Tax records

- **Types:** Property tax lists and poll tax records were kept at the town level in Massachusetts
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists are the primary substitute for the 1820 and 1830 censuses for individuals who don't appear as heads of household, and can track residency between census years
- **Access:** Town assessors' records; the Massachusetts_Land_and_Property and other specific topic pages returned only generic content, so no specific digitization details could be confirmed

### Other record types

- **Town meeting records:** Massachusetts towns maintained meeting records that name residents in connection with roads, poor relief, elections, and local ordinances — often unindexed but held by town clerks
- **Berkshire County court records:** County court minute books document civil and criminal proceedings, naming parties and witnesses. The Massachusetts Archives holds some older court records; the wiki_search result notes that "court records from the colonial period... document criminal proceedings, civil disputes, and administrative actions" at the Massachusetts Archives ([Massachusetts Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Military))
- **Town and county histories:** Published histories of Berkshire County towns from the 19th century often reprint early records and are sometimes the only surviving transcription of records since lost. NEHGS holds the largest genealogical library in the region (per wiki_search result)

## Repository guide

### Online repositories

| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Massachusetts, Town Vital Records 1620–1890 (3.4M records, collection 2061550); Massachusetts, Church Records 1630–1920 (987K records, collection 1921657); Massachusetts, Probate Records 1635–1991 (567K records, collection 1678901); Massachusetts, Naturalization Records 1790–1906 (345K records, collection 1459213); Massachusetts, Passenger Lists 1820–1891 (1.2M records, collection 1784312); browse-only volumes 004500891 (Town Clerk Vitals) and 004500892 (Pittsfield Congregational) | Free |
| Ancestry | U.S. Federal Census Collection (all census years 1820–1850) | Subscription |
| Fold3 | Military records (War of 1812, Mexican-American War) | Subscription |
| Newspapers.com | Historical newspapers including Berkshire County titles | Subscription |
| Find A Grave | Cemetery records | Free |
| NARA | Pension files, service records, passenger lists (originals) | Free / in-person |

**Coverage of this survey:** `volume_search` returned a complete result set of 2 digitized volumes for Berkshire County 1820–1850. Both are browse-only. The indexed collections above are at the Massachusetts state level and cover Berkshire County within them.

### Physical repositories

| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Berkshire County town clerks (each town) | Original birth, marriage, death records throughout the period; town meeting records | In-person / mail / some via state vital records office |
| Berkshire County Probate Court, Pittsfield | Wills, administrations, guardianships from 1761 | In-person / mail |
| Berkshire County Registry of Deeds, Pittsfield | Deeds and land records from 1761 | In-person; online index availability unconfirmed |
| Massachusetts Archives, Boston | Colony and state records; court records; state census (1855 and later); some military | In-person / online request |
| New England Historic Genealogical Society (NEHGS), Boston | Largest regional genealogical library; published vital records series; local histories | In-person; some online via American Ancestors subscription |
| Berkshire Athenaeum (Pittsfield Public Library) | Local histories, newspaper microfilm, Berkshire County records collection | In-person |
| Denominational archives | Church registers not yet microfilmed or digitized | Contact the specific denomination's archive |

## Records NOT online

- Town clerk vital records for most individual Berkshire County towns are not separately available as named online collections; they are reached through the Massachusetts, Town Vital Records 1620–1890 collection (2061550) which covers the state broadly. Physical originals remain with each town clerk
- County deed books (Berkshire County Registry of Deeds) — no digitized FamilySearch volumes or curated external collection for deeds was returned
- Town meeting records and assessors' tax lists — no digitized collection returned; held by individual town clerks
- Church records for denominations other than the Pittsfield Congregational congregation — the browse-only volume 004500892 covers only that one congregation; other congregations' records were not returned in the volume_search and may exist only in physical repositories or through the Massachusetts, Church Records collection (1921657) if included there
- War of 1812 pension case files — available at NARA physically; indexed versions accessible via Fold3

## Known record losses

No tool result in this survey stated that any specific Berkshire County record set was destroyed or lost. An absence of digitized volumes is a coverage gap, not evidence of destruction. Where a specific record class is missing online, the physical repository named above should be contacted before concluding a record does not exist.

## Research tips

- **Start with the published "Vital Records to 1850" series.** The wiki_search result confirms this series covers over 200 Massachusetts towns ([Massachusetts Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Genealogy#Colonial)). Many Berkshire County towns have published volumes in this series, and NEHGS or the Berkshire Athenaeum can confirm which towns are covered
- **For 1820–1841, treat the town clerk as the only vital-records authority.** The state system did not exist until 1841 (state level). Source: [Massachusetts Vital Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records). Do not assume the state system holds events before that date
- **Check both the bride's and groom's towns for marriage intentions.** The Massachusetts_Vital_Records page specifies that marriage intentions were commonly recorded in the bride's home town, with additional recordings possible in the groom's home town. If a marriage is not found in one town, search the other. Source: [Massachusetts Vital Records — FamilySearch Wiki](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Massachusetts_Vital_Records)
- **Search across the New York and Vermont borders.** Your family's town is near both state lines. Border families frequently generated records on both sides — church memberships, land purchases, and vital registrations could appear in adjacent New York or Vermont jurisdictions as well as in Berkshire County. The wiki_place_page home section returned only generic content, so the neighboring counties table was not available; identify the specific adjoining counties in New York (Columbia, Rensselaer, Washington) and Vermont (Bennington) and check their records if the Berkshire County record trail breaks off
- **The 1850 census is a turning point.** It is the first to name every household member rather than just the head; for this period, work backward from the 1850 record to establish the full household composition, then trace forward or backward through town vital records and church registers
- **Browse-only volumes require patience.** Both FamilySearch digitized volumes for this place (004500891 and 004500892) are 0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable. They must be opened and scrolled through image by image. If you know an approximate date and town or congregation, that narrows the browse. If you do not, the indexed Massachusetts, Town Vital Records collection (2061550) is the better first stop
- **FamilySearch Wiki pages for Massachusetts and Berkshire County returned only generic content** across two attempts during this survey. The specific Massachusetts_Genealogy, Massachusetts_Church_Records, Massachusetts_Land_and_Property, Massachusetts_Probate_Records, Massachusetts_Census, and Berkshire_County_Massachusetts_Genealogy pages all resolved to a generic fallback rather than their actual content. The Massachusetts_Vital_Records page was the exception. Re-visit those pages directly at FamilySearch.org before treating their absence as confirmed

---

Berkshire County, Massachusetts is a strong area for genealogical research in the 1820–1850 window. The most important thing to understand is that vital events — births, marriages, deaths — were recorded by each individual town, not by the county, and that a statewide system only came into being in 1841. For the first two decades of your window (1820–1841), the town clerk's office is the only civil authority that made these records, and published town-vital-records books are the fastest way to access what was recorded. Church registers, particularly Congregational ones, run alongside those town records and are essential cross-checks, especially since compliance with town-level recording was uneven. The family's proximity to the New York and Vermont borders means you should plan to search the adjacent counties in both states, not just Berkshire County — border families routinely left records in more than one state.

After reviewing this guide, the natural next step is building a research plan: identifying which specific towns in Berkshire County the family lived in, finding them in the 1850 census to anchor the household, then working backward town-record by town-record and church register by church register.

# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (1840–1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 1811 (FamilySearch place record dateRange "+1811/")
- **County seat / administrative center:** Not confirmed by any tool result returned in this survey
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Pennsylvania, United States
- **Population during period:** The place_population tool returned no data for this county and period
- **Economy:** Not stated by any returned tool result — the FamilySearch Wiki pages returned generic content
- **Ethnic composition:** Not stated by any returned tool result; a digitized church records volume (1842–1895, image group 007936751) is in English and German, indicating German-speaking congregations were present
- **Religious denominations:** Not stated by any returned tool result
- **Key historical events:** Not stated by any returned tool result

## Boundary changes
- place_search_all returned no additional historical representations for Schuylkill County, suggesting no boundary change records are stored in the FamilySearch place database for this county within the target period. The county has existed since 1811.
- If stable boundaries are confirmed by the county courthouse or state archives, state that boundaries were unchanged during 1840–1880.

## Available record types

Note: The FamilySearch Wiki pages for Schuylkill County (home section) and Pennsylvania (getting_started, online_records, research_tips sections) all returned the generic page at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Genealogy_Research_Guide during this survey rather than place-specific content. Claims below are grounded in MCP tool results only.

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Not stated by the FamilySearch Wiki vital records page — the Pennsylvania_Vital_Records URL redirected to a generic page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Genealogy_Records) with no Pennsylvania-specific registration dates.
- **What exists for 1840–1880:** 1 digitized volume of marriage records covering 1870–1910 (image group 007936753, 94 images), browse-only, 0% name-indexed. No digitized birth or death civil registration volumes appear for this period.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch — browse-only images (image group 007936753 for marriages 1870–1910)
- **Gaps:** No indexed vital records. Births and deaths are not represented in FamilySearch's digitized holdings for 1840–1880.
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church records (see below); federal census mortality schedules (1850, 1860, 1870, 1880 enumerations, recording deaths in the prior year); cemetery records.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Not confirmed by returned tool results. The language mix (English and German) in image group 007936751 indicates German-speaking congregations in the county.
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials
- **What exists:** 1 digitized volume covering 1842–1895 (image group 007936751, 187 images, English and German), browse-only, 0% name-indexed. FamilySearch collections_search also returned collection "SYNTH-PA-CHURCH" titled "Pennsylvania, Schuylkill County Church Records (synthetic test fixture)" (1708–1985, 1,245,830 records, 982,415 persons) — the "(synthetic test fixture)" label in the title indicates this is a test fixture rather than a verified production collection.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (image group 007936751, browse-only); denominational archives and local parishes for originals.
- **Language:** English and German (image group 007936751).

### Census records
- **Federal census:** Decennial censuses 1840–1880 cover Schuylkill County. The 1850 census for the county is confirmed available on Ancestry (indexed, https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/). Federal census records 1840–1880 are name-indexed on FamilySearch and Ancestry.
- **Mortality schedules:** Federal census mortality schedules (1850, 1860, 1870, 1880) record deaths in the year preceding the census — a source for death information when civil registration is absent.
- **State census:** No Pennsylvania state census volumes for 1840–1880 appear in volume_search results.
- **Other enumerations:** Pennsylvania Tax and Exoneration Lists 1768–1801 (Ancestry, https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/) — predates the target period but useful for earlier family traces.
- **Access:** FamilySearch (free) for indexed federal censuses; Ancestry (subscription) for the 1850 Schuylkill County census index.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, estate administrations, guardianships, inventories
- **Testate or intestate:** Search wills first; if none found, look for administrations (intestate).
- **What exists:** 1 digitized volume covering 1851–1930 (image group 007936749, 412 images), browse-only, 0% name-indexed. FamilySearch collection "Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994" (collection 1999196) covers this county with 3,200,560 images but 0 indexed records — browse-only.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (browse-only); Schuylkill County courthouse (originals).
- **Date range:** Digitized volume covers 1851–1930; broader holdings may exist at the county courthouse.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (Pennsylvania is not a federal land state; land grants originated with the colonial proprietors and later the Commonwealth).
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Not confirmed from returned tool results — the Pennsylvania Land and Property wiki page was not fetched in this survey.
- **Types:** Deeds
- **What exists:** 1 digitized volume of deed records covering 1815–1900 (image group 007936752, 543 images), 22% name-indexed — the only partially indexed volume in this county's FamilySearch holdings. The indexed portion is searchable by name; the remaining 78% must be browsed image by image.
- **Date range:** 1815–1900 for the digitized volume.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (image group 007936752, 22% indexed); Schuylkill County Recorder of Deeds for originals.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Mexican-American War (1846–1848) and Civil War (1861–1865) fall within or border the target period.
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files, bounty land warrants, draft registrations.
- **Where held:** National Archives and Records Administration (NARA). No Schuylkill County–specific military volumes appear in the FamilySearch volume_search results; use FamilySearch's national Civil War collections and NARA's indexed military pension and service record databases.
- **Access:** FamilySearch national Civil War collections (free); Fold3 for detailed military records (subscription).

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Not stated by any returned tool result.
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (https://www.findagrave.com) and BillionGraves provide online headstone transcriptions for many Pennsylvania cemeteries; check both for Schuylkill County. No cemetery-specific volumes appear in the volume_search results.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and burial registers may be held by individual congregations or cemeteries; no specific holdings confirmed by tool results.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Not stated by any returned tool result — wiki pages returned generic content.
- **Where held:** Pennsylvania State Archives, local libraries, and national digital archives. Chronicling America (https://chroniclingamerica.loc.gov) covers some Pennsylvania papers in the period.
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, legal notices (estate sales, sheriff's sales).

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Philadelphia (closest major port); New York and Baltimore also served Pennsylvania immigrants.
- **Record types:** Passenger arrival manifests; naturalization records (declarations of intention, petitions).
- **What exists:** 1 digitized volume of naturalization records covering 1849–1915 (image group 007936750, 298 images), browse-only, 0% name-indexed. Pre-1906 naturalizations could be filed in any court of record, including Schuylkill County courts.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch (browse-only, image group 007936750); NARA for passenger lists and post-1906 naturalization records.
- **Content note:** Passenger lists (arrival manifests) record every person aboard, including infants and young children traveling with parents. When researching a family, examine the full manifest for all family members — children as young as newborns are listed.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Property tax, personal property, poll tax
- **Date range:** Pennsylvania Tax and Exoneration Lists on Ancestry cover 1768–1801 (pre-period). No county-level tax volumes for 1840–1880 appear in the FamilySearch volume_search results.
- **Where held:** Schuylkill County; Pennsylvania State Archives. Physical records for 1840–1880 are not represented in FamilySearch's digitized holdings for this county.
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists substitute for missing census years and document residence between censuses.

### Other record types
- **Court records:** Schuylkill County Court of Common Pleas held naturalization cases and civil/criminal proceedings. No court-record-specific volumes beyond probate appear in volume_search results for 1840–1880.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Deed Records 1815–1900 (image group 007936752, 22% indexed, 543 images); Probate Records 1851–1930 (browse-only, 007936749, 412 images); Naturalization Records 1849–1915 (browse-only, 007936750, 298 images); Church Records 1842–1895 (browse-only, English/German, 007936751, 187 images); Marriage Records 1870–1910 (browse-only, 007936753, 94 images); Pennsylvania Probate Records 1683–1994 (collection 1999196, 3,200,560 images, browse-only); federal census indexes 1840–1880 | Free |
| Ancestry | 1850 United States Federal Census — Schuylkill County (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/); Pennsylvania Tax and Exoneration Lists 1768–1801 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/7667/) | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** 5 digitized volumes match Schuylkill County for 1840–1880 — this is the complete result set (volume_search totalResults: 5, summary complete: true; all 5 are detailed above).

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Schuylkill County Courthouse | Deed records, probate files, court records, marriage licenses (originals) | In-person / mail request |
| Pennsylvania State Archives | State-level records, military records, tax records | In-person / written request |
| National Archives (Philadelphia region) | Federal census originals, military records, post-1906 naturalization records | In-person / online request |
| Local historical/genealogical societies | Transcriptions, cemetery surveys, manuscript collections | Contact directly |

## Records NOT online
- **Probate records:** Collection 1999196 (3,200,560 images, 1683–1994) is browse-only; not name-indexed.
- **Church records** (image group 007936751, 1842–1895): browse-only, in English and German; not name-indexed.
- **Naturalization records** (image group 007936750, 1849–1915): browse-only; not name-indexed.
- **Marriage records** (image group 007936753, 1870–1910): browse-only; not name-indexed.
- **Birth and death civil registrations for 1840–1880:** No digitized volumes appear in this survey; these records (if they exist for this period) are not represented in FamilySearch's digitized holdings for this county.
- **Tax records 1840–1880:** No county-level volumes for this period appear in FamilySearch.
- **Military records specific to Schuylkill County:** No county-level military volumes appear; use national collections.

## Known record losses
No tool result returned in this survey states that any specific Schuylkill County record set was destroyed or lost. An absence of digitized volumes is a coverage gap, not evidence the records do not exist. Contact the Schuylkill County courthouse and the Pennsylvania State Archives to confirm physical holdings and their condition.

## Research tips
- The FamilySearch Wiki pages for Schuylkill County and Pennsylvania returned generic content (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Genealogy_Research_Guide) rather than place-specific guidance during this survey. Visit wiki.familysearch.org directly and search for "Schuylkill County Pennsylvania" and "Pennsylvania Vital Records" to check for updated pages.
- The only partially indexed FamilySearch volume for 1840–1880 is Deed Records 1815–1900 (image group 007936752, 22% name-indexed, 543 images). All other digitized volumes must be browsed image by image with no name index — plan time accordingly.
- Church records are likely the primary source for vital events (births, marriages, deaths) during 1840–1880, as civil registration for the target period is not reflected in FamilySearch's holdings. The digitized church volume (image group 007936751, 1842–1895) includes German-language records — be prepared to read German.
- Pre-1906 naturalization records could be filed in any court of record. Search the Schuylkill County naturalization volume (image group 007936750, 1849–1915, browse-only) alongside NARA's online indexes and Philadelphia-area federal court records.
- Federal census mortality schedules (1850, 1860, 1870, 1880) record deaths in the prior year and substitute for missing death registrations. Search these alongside standard census enumerations.
- The 1850 census for Schuylkill County is indexed and available on both FamilySearch and Ancestry (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1276/); cross-reference both for transcription accuracy.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

> **Survey note:** Most FamilySearch wiki and place-search tools returned only placeholder content or empty results during this survey. The guide below is sourced primarily from the Ireland Church Records wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records), the one page that returned full content. All repository and collection details not from that page are from known published sources. Re-run this guide when the tool layer is restored before relying on any absence noted here.

---

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, barony of Cary, County Antrim, Province of Ulster
- **Town of interest:** Bushmills
- **Post-1922 status:** County Antrim remained in the United Kingdom (Northern Ireland) after Irish partition. Records are primarily at the **Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI)** in Belfast, not the National Archives of Ireland in Dublin — though some pre-1922 national records appear in both.
- **Religious composition (1861 census):** Church of Ireland and Presbyterian together ~60%; Catholic ~40%. This is crucial for identifying which church registers to search.

---

## Record Types Available

### Church Records — The Core Source for 1780–1870

Civil registration did not begin until **1 January 1864**, so church records are the primary source for the entire target period.

**Church of Ireland (Anglican)**

The direct answer to your question: **approximately two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers were destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin.** Whether Billy parish's specific registers survived depends on whether they had been sent to Dublin before the fire.

- The definitive answer is in **PRONI's Guide to Church Records**: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf — this lists exactly which churches in each civil parish have surviving registers and whether PRONI holds them on microfilm or as originals.
- **PRONI's digitised church records:** https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1
- **RCB Library** (Representative Church Body Library), Dublin, holds the Church of Ireland's own register collection. Their parish register list (https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf) will confirm whether a copy of Billy's registers is held there.
- **FamilySearch — Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866** (collection 3460239) — free, covers Church of Ireland marriages including County Antrim.
- **FindMyPast — Ffolliott Collection** (index): Church of Ireland baptisms, confirmations, marriages, and burials for the Diocese of Connor (which covers County Antrim).

**Presbyterian**

- County Antrim had a very strong Presbyterian presence (17th-century Plantation of Ulster settlers from Scotland).
- Presbyterian registers were **not deposited in Dublin** and were therefore **unaffected by the 1922 fire**. PRONI holds a substantial collection.
- Average register start date is around 1830; some date from the 1600s, but many County Antrim congregations' registers begin between 1810–1840.
- **FindMyPast — Ireland Non-Conformist Births and Baptisms:** https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms

**Catholic**

- Most rural parishes did not begin keeping registers until Catholic Emancipation in **1828**. Some records exist from the mid-1700s, but the 1780–1828 segment is sparse.
- **National Library of Ireland — free digitised images of Catholic parish registers:** https://registers.nli.ie/
- **Ancestry — Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915** (collection 61039, subscription)
- Note: Catholic parish boundaries do not align with civil parish boundaries. Identify the correct Catholic parish for Billy/Bushmills separately.

---

### Civil Registration (1864–1870 only)

- Births, marriages, and deaths for all denominations were recorded from 1 January 1864.
- Relevant registration district: likely **Ballycastle** or **Coleraine** — confirm with GRONI.
- **General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI)**, Colby House, Stranmillis Court, Belfast BT9 5RR — index searchable at nidirect.gov.uk/gro.

---

### Census Records

A major record loss. The 1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 returns for most of Ireland (including County Antrim) were destroyed in the 1922 fire. The 1861 and 1871 originals were separately destroyed by government order. **No census survives for the 1780–1870 target window.**

**Substitute census sources:**
- **Tithe Applotment Books, 1823–1837** — survey of land for tithe calculation; names householders by townland. Essential.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation, 1847–1864** — comprehensive valuation of all rateable property, naming occupier and landlord. Freely searchable at http://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/ and IrishOrigins.com (subscription).

---

### Land Records

| Record | Dates | Where held |
|---|---|---|
| Tithe Applotment Books | 1823–1837 | NAI; digitised/indexed on multiple sites |
| Griffith's Primary Valuation | 1847–1864 | AskAboutIreland (free); IrishOrigins (subscription) |
| Registry of Deeds (transfers, leases, mortgages) | From 1708 | Registry of Deeds, Dublin; PRONI transcripts |
| Estate papers (rentals, leases naming tenants) | Varies | PRONI — not systematically digitised |

---

### Probate Records

- Pre-1858 ecclesiastical probate (Diocese of Connor for County Antrim) records were destroyed in the 1922 fire. Surviving abstracts and indexes compensate partially:
  - **Betham Genealogical Abstracts** (FindMyPast) — abstracts from pre-1922 records including will abstracts
  - **Thrift Genealogical Abstracts** (FindMyPast) — wills, parish registers, pedigree charts
  - **Crossle Genealogical Abstracts** (FindMyPast)
  - **Ancestry — Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866** (collection 62077)
- Post-1858 civil probate: Belfast district registry covered County Antrim. Original wills held at PRONI.

---

### Military Records

- British Army service records and pension files: **The National Archives (UK), Kew** — partially digitised on FindMyPast and Ancestry (WO 97 series for other-rank discharges).
- Antrim Militia muster rolls: PRONI.

---

### Newspapers

| Paper | Dates | Access |
|---|---|---|
| *Belfast News-Letter* | From 1737 | British Newspaper Archive (findmypast.com) |
| *Northern Whig* (Belfast) | From 1821 | British Newspaper Archive |
| *Coleraine Chronicle* | From 1844 | British Newspaper Archive; Linen Hall Library |

Useful for obituaries, marriage notices, estate sale announcements, and tenant-eviction proceedings.

---

### Other Records

- **School registers (from 1831):** PRONI; some indexed by Ulster Historical Foundation. Names children and sometimes parents with addresses — useful for birth dates.
- **Freeholders'/voters' lists:** PRONI — name men of property with voting rights.
- **Town directories** (Pigot's 1820s, Slater's): name householders and tradespeople in Bushmills. Partial digitisation on Internet Archive.

- **Check PRONI's Guide to Church Records first** — this is the single most important step for answering whether Church of Ireland registers survive for Billy/Bushmills.

# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Ireland (1780–1870)

> **Survey note:** During this survey, `place_search` returned empty results for all queries, including "Ireland" itself. `collections_search`, `volume_search`, and all four `wiki_place_page` sections resolved to empty standard places and returned no results. The vast majority of `wiki_read` requests returned only a generic placeholder rather than the requested page. The one exception is the Ireland Church Records wiki page at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records, which returned full content and is the primary cited source throughout this guide. All FamilySearch wiki sections listed in `pages_read` are therefore marked `found: false` with `outcome: "unreachable"` for this survey. Re-run this locality guide before relying on the absence of any specific collection or collection date.

---

## Jurisdiction overview

- **Civil parish:** Billy, barony of Cary, County Antrim, Province of Ulster
- **Town of interest:** Bushmills
- **Parent jurisdiction (national):** From 1801, County Antrim was within the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland. After 1922, it remained in the United Kingdom as part of Northern Ireland. Per the Ireland Church Records wiki page, "six of the nine counties forming the province of Ulster (Antrim, Armagh, Down, Fermanagh, Londonderry, and Tyrone) voted to remain part of the United Kingdom" when the Republic of Ireland was created. This administrative split is critical: records created after 1922 for County Antrim are in Northern Ireland repositories, not the Republic's archives; records up to 1922 may appear in both.
- **Population during period:** Population figures were not returned by any tool during this survey. The 1861 census (a known source) enumerated a population for County Antrim, but no specific figure was returned.
- **Religious composition:** Per the Ireland Church Records wiki page, in Northern Ireland in 1861, "the Church of Ireland and various aspects of the Presbyterian Churches were the dominant religions, accounting for sixty-percent of the population... While Catholics were a minority, they accounted for forty-percent of the population." This was broadly true of rural County Antrim throughout 1780–1870.
- **Economy:** County Antrim in this period was agricultural (small tenant farms), with linen manufacture. The Bushmills/Cary area was rural coastal — no tool data returned specific figures.

## Boundary changes

- Billy civil parish boundaries were stable in this period under the administrative structure of County Antrim, barony of Cary.
- The key administrative split is 1922: pre-1922, records were overseen from Dublin (Public Record Office of Ireland, now NAI); post-1922, records are split between the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI) in Belfast and the National Archives of Ireland (NAI) in Dublin. Copies of many national records up to 1922 are available in both, per the Ireland Church Records wiki page.

---

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)

- **Start date:** Civil registration of births, marriages, and deaths for all denominations began on **1 January 1864** across Ireland (all-island, state level). Per the Ireland Church Records wiki page, "Before civil registration was introduced in 1864, Church records provide the primary source for providing baptism, marriage and burial dates." For 1780–1864 — the majority of the target window — there are no civil vital records. Only the last six years of the target period (1864–1870) are covered by civil registration.
- **What exists (1864–1870):** Births, marriages, and deaths registered at the civil registration district level. The relevant district for Bushmills/Billy is the Ballycastle registration district (or Coleraine — the researcher should confirm the district assignment from the General Register Office).
- **Where held:** For Northern Ireland, civil registration records are held by the **General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI)**, Colby House, Stranmillis Court, Belfast BT9 5RR. Indexes are available online at nidirect.gov.uk/gro. The original registers are also searchable via PRONI.
- **Gaps:** Effectively complete gap for 1780–1863 in civil records. Church records fill this gap (see below).
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church baptism, marriage, and burial registers are the primary source for 1780–1863. Land and tax records supplement these for establishing residence and approximate age.

### Church records

This is the **most important record class for 1780–1870** in Billy civil parish.

**Church of Ireland (Anglican/Episcopal)**
- Per the Ireland Church Records wiki page, "Church of Ireland Records began in 1536, but two-thirds were destroyed in 1922." The 1922 destruction occurred when the Public Record Office of Ireland in Dublin burned during the Irish Civil War. Registers that had been deposited in Dublin before 1922 were lost; registers that remained in the local parish or were held by diocesan bodies survived or were microfilmed.
- For Billy/Bushmills specifically: Whether the Church of Ireland registers for Billy parish survived depends on whether they had been sent to Dublin before 1922. The authoritative source for this is **PRONI's Guide to Church Records** (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf), which lists exactly what churches exist in each civil parish, what records exist, and whether PRONI holds them on microfilm or as originals. The researcher must consult that guide directly to determine which registers, if any, survive for Billy parish and what years they cover. Digitised church records available through PRONI are listed at: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1
- The **RCB Library** (Representative Church Body Library), Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14, D14 N735 (library@ireland.anglican.org) holds the Church of Ireland's own register collection. Their complete parish register list is at https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf — this list will show whether RCB holds a copy of Billy's registers.
- Church of Ireland records for the Diocese of Connor (which covers County Antrim) that are available through the **Ffolliott Collection** on FindMyPast include baptisms, confirmations, marriages, and burials: https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/irish-parish-register-baptisms-and-confirmations-ffolliott-collection (index only, subscription).
- **Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866** are available at FamilySearch (collection 3460239, index and images, free): https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239. These cover Church of Ireland marriages and are relevant for the Billy/Bushmills area.

**Presbyterian**
- County Antrim had a very strong Presbyterian presence owing to the 17th-century plantation. Per the Ireland Church Records wiki page, "In 1605 Scottish estate owners resettled mostly Presbyterian tenants from their estates to newly established estates in Northern Ireland. Numerous registers date from the 1600s, but the average starting date for these registers is 1830." For Billy parish in the 1780–1830 period, Presbyterian registers may be absent or sparse.
- Presbyterian registers were not deposited in Dublin and therefore were **not affected by the 1922 fire**. PRONI holds a substantial collection. The PRONI Guide to Church Records identifies the specific Presbyterian congregations in Billy/Bushmills and what years their registers cover.
- **Non-Conformist records** (including Presbyterian) on FindMyPast: https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms (index, subscription).

**Catholic**
- Per the Ireland Church Records wiki page, "Ireland Catholic Church Records began from the mid 1700s. Most rural parishes did not start keeping records until Catholic Emancipation in 1828." For the 1780–1828 period, Catholic registers for Billy/Bushmills may be absent or start late.
- **Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915** at Ancestry (collection 61039), index and images, subscription: https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/61039/
- Catholic registers are also available through the **National Library of Ireland** at https://registers.nli.ie/ — this free resource has digitised images of Catholic parish registers.
- Catholic and Presbyterian parish boundaries do not align with civil parish (Church of Ireland) boundaries. The researcher should identify the appropriate Catholic parish serving Billy/Bushmills separately from the civil parish structure.

**Language:** Records for 1780–1870 in County Antrim are in English. Latin was used in some earlier Catholic registers but is uncommon by this period.

### Census records

- **Irish census records are a major loss.** The 1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 census returns for most of Ireland, including County Antrim, were destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire. Some fragments and transcripts survive. The 1861 and 1871 originals were officially destroyed by government order in the early 20th century. No tool data was returned confirming specific surviving fragments for Billy/Bushmills.
- **1901 and 1911 census:** Fully surviving and online (outside the 1780–1870 window, but useful for tracing families backward). Available free at the National Archives of Ireland: http://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/
- **Substitute census sources for 1780–1870:**
  - Tithe Applotment Books, 1823–1837 (see Land records below)
  - Griffith's Valuation, 1847–1864 (see Land records below)
  - Church census/vestry records where they survive

### Probate and court records

- **Ecclesiastical probate** (Prerogative and Diocesan courts) operated before 1858. County Antrim fell under the Diocese of Connor for most probate purposes. A major loss: original wills and administration bonds proved in these courts before 1858 were destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin. However, indexes and abstracts survive.
- **Betham Genealogical Abstracts** on FindMyPast (https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/betham-genealogical-abstracts): genealogical abstracts from many pre-1922 records, including will abstracts, described by the Ireland Church Records wiki page as "useful substitute to records lost in the 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin."
- **Thrift Genealogical Abstracts** on FindMyPast (https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/thrift-genealogical-abstracts): include wills, parish registers, and pedigree charts going back to the 16th century.
- **Crossle Genealogical Abstracts** on FindMyPast (https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/crossle-genealogical-abstracts): genealogical records collected by Dr. Francis Crossle.
- **Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866** at Ancestry (collection 62077): index and images, subscription.
- After 1858, civil probate operated from the Principal Probate Registry in Dublin and district registries. The Belfast district registry covered County Antrim. Post-1858 wills are more likely to survive. PRONI holds the original wills for Northern Ireland.
- Testacy vs. intestacy: Those who left wills had them proved in the ecclesiastical or civil probate courts above; those who died intestate generated letters of administration in the same courts.

### Land records

- **Tithe Applotment Books, 1823–1837:** A survey of land to calculate tithes owed to the Church of Ireland. Covers County Antrim, including Billy parish. These are name-rich and function as a partial census substitute. Available at the NAI and digitised/indexed at various sites. FamilySearch has the Tithe Applotment books on microfilm for many counties.
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864):** A county-by-county valuation of all rateable property, naming the occupier and the landlord. County Antrim was surveyed in this period. This is an **essential** substitute census for the period. Freely searchable at AskAboutIreland: http://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/ and at IrishOrigins.com (subscription).
- **Registry of Deeds, Dublin (from 1708):** Records transfers of land, leases, and mortgages for all of Ireland. The Registry of Deeds Indexes are searchable. PRONI holds transcripts.
- **Estate papers:** Many County Antrim families were tenants on large estates. Estate papers (rentals, leases, correspondence naming tenants) can survive in PRONI and are often not digitised.
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds. Land-distribution jurisdiction for County Antrim was under the Crown (via the Ulster plantation grants, then private landlords). The Registry of Deeds in Dublin handled formal registration.

### Military records

- **Relevant conflicts:** The 1798 United Irishmen rebellion affected County Antrim directly (Battle of Antrim, June 1798). Some Antrim men served in the British Army in the Napoleonic Wars and later in the Crimean War and Indian Mutiny.
- **Record types:** British Army service records and pension files are held at **The National Archives (UK)** in Kew, London. Many are indexed and digitised at FindMyPast and Ancestry. The **WO 97** series holds soldiers' documents for other-rank discharges.
- **Militia records:** The Antrim Militia was active in this period. Militia muster rolls may survive at PRONI.
- **Pension records:** Chelsea and Kilmainham Hospital pension records for Irish soldiers are at the National Archives (UK), partially digitised.

### Cemetery records

- **Major cemeteries:** Billy parish contains the old churchyard at Bushmills (Church of Ireland) and other local burial grounds. No specific cemetery data was returned by any tool during this survey.
- **Online coverage:** The Ulster Historical Foundation's AncestryIreland site (http://www.ancestryireland.com/) and RootsIreland (https://www.rootsireland.ie/) contain some County Antrim cemetery transcriptions. FindAGrave and BillionGraves have varying Ulster coverage but no specific Billy/Bushmills data was confirmed.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records where they survive are held with the parish (PRONI or local).

### Newspaper records

- **Local papers:** The *Coleraine Chronicle* (from 1844) and *Northern Whig* (Belfast, from 1821) are the most relevant papers for the Bushmills/Cary area in this period. The *Belfast News-Letter* dates from 1737 and is the oldest surviving newspaper in continuous publication in the British Isles.
- **Where held:** British Newspaper Archive (findmypast.com) has digitised many Ulster newspapers. The Linen Hall Library in Belfast and the British Library hold physical runs.
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, tenant eviction notices, criminal proceedings, and land sale notices.

### Immigration/emigration records

- County Antrim experienced substantial emigration throughout 1780–1870, peaking during and after the Famine (1845–1852). Many emigrants went to North America via ports at Londonderry/Derry, Belfast, Liverpool, and Glasgow.
- **Relevant ports:** Derry/Londonderry was the primary emigration port for northwest Ulster. Belfast was also used. Most westbound traffic went to Quebec, New York, Philadelphia, or Boston.
- **Record types:**
  - Passenger lists (departure and arrival manifests)
  - **Inland records:** Declarations of intention and naturalization petitions were filed in US courts wherever the immigrant settled — these are not confined to ports.
  - **Emigrant lists:** Some estate papers at PRONI record assisted emigration by landlords, naming individual tenants.
- **Ireland, Emigration and Immigration wiki page** is at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Emigration_and_Immigration (this URL returned only a generic placeholder during this survey — consult it directly after re-running the survey).
- Passenger lists note: Manifests record every person aboard including infants. When searching a family, examine the full manifest for all members.

### Tax records

- **Hearth Money Rolls (1660s):** Earlier than the target window, but useful for establishing family presence.
- **Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837):** Already listed under land records; primary tax substitute for census.
- **Griffith's Valuation (1847–1864):** Already listed under land records; functions as a comprehensive property tax list and population substitute.
- **County cess/grand jury records:** County Antrim grand jury presentments are held at PRONI and name taxpayers, road contractors, and petitioners.
- **Where held:** PRONI for Northern Ireland tax records.

### Other record types

- **School records:** Ireland's National School system was established in 1831. School registers survive for many County Antrim schools at PRONI. These name children and sometimes list parents and addresses — valuable for dates of birth.
- **Freeholders' lists:** County Antrim freeholders' and voters' lists survive for various years and are held at PRONI. These name men of property who had voting rights.
- **Town directories:** Pigot's Directory (1820s) and later Slater's Directory covered County Antrim, including Bushmills. These name householders and tradespeople.
- **Ulster Historical Foundation:** Specialises in Ulster genealogy; holds indexes and published volumes for County Antrim (http://www.ancestryireland.com/).

## Records NOT online

The following exist but are not fully (or not at all) available online:

- **Full Church of Ireland parish registers** for Billy/Bushmills — PRONI holds what survives; whether any are digitised online must be checked at https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/articles/digitised-church-records-available-proni#toc-1
- **Estate papers** naming individual tenant families — held physically at PRONI; not systematically digitised
- **Grand jury/county cess records** — physical at PRONI
- **School registers** (from 1831) — physical at PRONI; some indexed by Ulster Historical Foundation
- **Freeholders' and voters' lists** — physical at PRONI
- **Town directories** (original runs) — partial digitisation at British Newspaper Archive and Internet Archive
- **Militia muster rolls** — physical at PRONI

## Known record losses

Per the Ireland Church Records wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records):

- **The 1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin** destroyed approximately two-thirds of Church of Ireland parish registers that had been deposited there, along with original pre-1858 ecclesiastical probate records (wills, administration bonds, marriage license bonds). The Betham, Crossle, and Thrift genealogical abstracts on FindMyPast partially compensate for the lost probate material.
- **The 1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 Irish census returns** were destroyed in the same 1922 fire, with some fragments surviving. The 1861 and 1871 originals were separately destroyed by government order. No specific surviving fragment data for Billy parish was confirmed by tools in this survey.
- Whether the Church of Ireland registers for **Billy/Bushmills specifically** survived the 1922 fire cannot be confirmed without checking PRONI's Guide to Church Records (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) and the RCB Library's parish register list.

## Research tips

The following are sourced from the Ireland Church Records wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records). Other Ireland-specific wiki pages (Ireland Civil Registration, Ireland Land and Property, Ireland Census, County Antrim Genealogy, Ireland Research Tips and Strategies) returned only a generic placeholder during this survey — consult them directly at familysearch.org/wiki.

- **Check Church of Ireland registers even for non-Church of Ireland families.** Per the Ireland Church Records wiki page: "Search available Church of Ireland records even if your family was not of the Church of Ireland." Before 1864, Church of Ireland registers served as de facto civil records; Catholics and Presbyterians sometimes appear in Church of Ireland marriage records particularly (required for legal purposes under certain periods of the Marriage Acts).
- **Identify the denomination before searching.** A Catholic family, a Presbyterian family, and a Church of Ireland family in Bushmills in 1830 generated records in completely different repositories. The Ireland Church Records wiki page stresses: "Identifying the religion of those individuals or families being researched will greatly increase the chance of success."
- **Catholic and Presbyterian parish boundaries do not follow civil parish lines.** A family in Billy civil parish may belong to a Catholic or Presbyterian parish whose boundary cuts differently. Search surrounding localities' registers if the expected register has gaps.
- **Note gaps in registers.** When a gap appears in a church register, check whether a different denomination's register covers the same years — families sometimes appear in neighbouring church records during the gap.
- **Griffith's Valuation and Tithe Applotment together substitute for the lost censuses.** Use Tithe Applotment (1823–1837) for the earlier end and Griffith's (1847–1864) for the later end of the target window to anchor a family in a specific townland.
- **The Ulster Historical Foundation (ancestryireland.com)** specialises in County Antrim and neighbouring Ulster counties. For Antrim research, check their published county indexes before searching general databases.
- **Search adjoining parishes.** Billy civil parish borders other Antrim parishes to the east and south, and County Londonderry/Derry lies to the west across the River Bann. Families near the Bann may have generated records on the Londonderry side. Check both county repositories (PRONI covers both) and the Diocese of Londonderry's church records as well as the Diocese of Connor.

output.text_response:
# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction Overview

- **Location:** Barony of Lower Dunluce (chiefly) and barony of Carey, poor law union of Coleraine, County Antrim, Province of Ulster. Main settlement: Bushmills.
- **Post-1922:** County Antrim remained in Northern Ireland (UK). The primary archive is **PRONI** (Belfast), not the National Archives of Ireland in Dublin.
- **Denominations present:** Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, Covenanting (Reformed Presbyterian), Wesleyan Methodist, and Catholic.

---

## The Core Gap: Church Register Coverage

The [FamilySearch Wiki page for Billy Civil Parish](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy) lists all denominations (Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, Covenanter, Methodist, Catholic) but every sub-section is **empty** — no register start dates, no PRONI microfilm numbers, and no collection IDs. Civil registration only began in 1864, leaving 1780–1863 almost entirely dependent on church registers. Closing that gap requires consulting the repositories below directly.

---

## By Denomination

### Church of Ireland
- Billy was formerly the **head of an ecclesiastical union** comprising Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride. Registers for the union period may be catalogued under any of those parishes. Search all five.
- ~Two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers were destroyed in the **1922 Public Record Office fire in Dublin**. Whether Billy's registers survived is not confirmed in any online source — PRONI and the RCB Library must be consulted.
- **PRONI Guide to Church Records** (free PDF): https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf — the definitive finding aid for which registers survive, their PRONI MIC reference numbers, and whether they are digitized.
- **RCB Library** (holds registers not at PRONI): search at https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy; downloadable Parish Register list at https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf

### Presbyterian & Covenanting
- Billy parish had meeting houses for both groups. Presbyterian registers in Ireland typically begin around 1830, though some date to the 1600s.
- Original registers are often held by the local congregation; PRONI holds microfilm copies for many County Antrim congregations.
- **PRONI Guide to Church Records** (same PDF above) will identify which Bushmills-area congregations have deposited records and their film numbers.
- Online: **Ulster Historical Foundation** (https://www.ancestryireland.com/), **RootsIreland** (https://www.rootsireland.ie/), and **FindMyPast** – Ireland, Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms / Marriages / Burials (subscription, https://www.findmypast.com).

### Catholic
- Billy parish is part of the **Catholic district of Coleraine** — search Coleraine-district registers, not a Billy-specific set.
- Most rural Catholic parishes did not begin registers until after Catholic Emancipation (1828), so pre-1828 coverage will likely be sparse or absent.
- **National Library of Ireland** (free images): https://registers.nli.ie/
- **Ancestry** – Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915 (collection/61039, subscription)

### Wesleyan Methodist
- A meeting house is confirmed in the parish; no register start date is listed in any available source.
- **FindMyPast** – Ireland, Non-Conformist Congregational Records (subscription): https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-congregational-records
- **PRONI Guide** will identify any deposited registers.

---

## Civil Registration (1864–1870 only)
- Civil registration of all births, marriages, and deaths began **1 January 1864**; non-Catholic marriages from **1 April 1845**.
- **GRONI** (General Register Office Northern Ireland): Oxford House, 49–55 Chichester Street, Belfast BT1 4HL; Tel: 028 9025 2000; https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/contacts/contacts-az/general-register-office-northern-ireland
- **IrishGenealogy.ie** (free civil registration indexes): https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/en/

---

## Census Substitutes (Pre-1901)
Most pre-1901 Antrim census returns were destroyed. The key substitutes for the target window are:
- **Tithe Applotment Books 1823–1837** – FamilySearch collection (free): https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1823694
- **Griffith's Primary Valuation 1847–1864** – free at https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/ and https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/

---

## Newspapers
- **Belfast News-Letter** (est. 1737) and **Coleraine Chronicle** (est. 1844) carry obituaries, marriage notices, and legal notices.
- Searchable at: **British Newspaper Archive** (https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/, subscription) and **FindMyPast** (subscription).

---

## Repository Guide

| Repository | What it holds for Billy parish | Address / URL |
|---|---|---|
| **PRONI** | Church register microfilms for all Antrim denominations; estate papers; Tithe Applotment; probate from 1858; yeomanry & militia | 2 Titanic Blvd, Belfast BT3 9HQ; proni@communities-ni.gov.uk; https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/proni |
| **RCB Library** | Surviving Church of Ireland registers not held at PRONI | Braemor Park, Churchtown, Dublin 14; library@ireland.anglican.org; https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy |
| **GRONI** | Civil registration births, marriages, deaths from 1864 | Oxford House, 49–55 Chichester Street, Belfast BT1 4HL; https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/contacts/contacts-az/general-register-office-northern-ireland |
| **NLI** (National Library of Ireland) | Catholic parish register images (free) | https://registers.nli.ie/ |
| **National Archives of Ireland** | Civil registration indexes to 1922; some Catholic records | Bishop Street, Dublin D08 DF85; https://www.nationalarchives.ie/ |
| **Ulster Historical Foundation** | Indexed County Antrim church records by denomination | https://www.ancestryireland.com/ |
| **RootsIreland** | Indexed Irish church records by county | https://www.rootsireland.ie/ |
| **FamilySearch** | Ireland, Diocesan & Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes 1623–1866 (collection/3460239); Tithe Applotment Books | https://www.familysearch.org |
| **Ancestry** | Ireland Catholic Parish Registers 1655–1915 (collection/61039); Indexes to Wills, Probate & Marriage Bonds 1591–1866 (collection/62077) | https://www.ancestry.com |
| **FindMyPast** | Non-Conformist registers (births, marriages, burials, congregational records); Ffolliott Collection; Betham/Crossle/Thrift abstracts | https://www.findmypast.com |
| **British Newspaper Archive** | Belfast News-Letter, Coleraine Chronicle, Ulster papers | https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/ |
| **Causeway Coast & Glens Borough Council** | Local history, graveyard surveys for North Antrim | Cloonavin, 66 Portstewart Rd, Coleraine BT52 1EY |

---

## Recommended First Steps to Close the Gap

1. **Download the PRONI Guide to Church Records** (PDF linked above) and look up Billy parish *and* all five parishes of the former ecclesiastical union (Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, Kilbride) for every denomination. This tells you exactly what survives, what dates it covers, and whether it is on microfilm or digitized.
2. **Search registers.nli.ie** for the Coleraine Catholic district (not "Billy") — covers post-1828 Catholic events.
3. **Check the RCB Library's Parish Register list** to confirm whether any Billy Church of Ireland registers survived 1922.
4. **Run the Ulster Historical Foundation and RootsIreland indexes** for County Antrim to pick up indexed Presbyterian and non-conformist entries.
5. **Use Griffith's Valuation and Tithe Applotment Books** as the primary household locators for 1823–1864, bridging the worst gap in church-register coverage.
