# Locality Guide: Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim (1780–1870)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Ancient civil parish; situated partly in the barony of Carey and chiefly in the barony of Lower Dunluce, poor law union of Coleraine, County Antrim, Province of Ulster. (Source: [Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy))
- **Main settlements:** Bushmills (post town) and a portion of Dunserverick.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** County Antrim, Province of Ulster. County Antrim is one of the six counties that remained in the United Kingdom as Northern Ireland in 1922; primary archive is therefore the Public Record Office of Northern Ireland (PRONI), not the National Archives of Ireland in Dublin.
- **Population during period:** The tools were unable to return population figures for this place (the place_search and place_population tools returned no results for any Irish locality). Contemporary population figures appear in the Parliamentary Gazetteer of Ireland (various editions 1844–1846), held at PRONI and available on Archive.org.
- **Economy:** Linen weaving, small farming, fishing, and distilling (Bushmills Distillery operating in this period).
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly Ulster Scots (Presbyterian and Covenanting) descent, with a minority Catholic and Church of Ireland population.
- **Religious denominations:** The 1861 census of Ireland reported the Church of Ireland and various Presbyterian churches together accounted for approximately 60% of Northern Ireland's population; Catholics approximately 40%. For Billy parish specifically, the FamilySearch Wiki confirms meeting houses for Presbyterians, Covenanters, and Wesleyan Methodists, alongside an implied Church of Ireland presence (the parish was formerly the ecclesiastical head of a union) and a Catholic population served by the district of Coleraine. (Source: [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))
- **Key historical events:** The Great Famine (1845–1852) caused population loss through death and mass emigration from the whole of Ulster. The 1798 United Irishmen rebellion affected County Antrim directly (the Battle of Antrim was fought in June 1798). Both events have implications for which records survive and what gaps appear.

## Boundary changes
- Billy parish's civil boundaries were stable across 1780–1870. No sub-division is noted in the FamilySearch Wiki.
- The ecclesiastical geography is more complex: Billy was formerly the head of a Church of Ireland ecclesiastical union comprising the parishes of Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride. After this union was dissolved, Church of Ireland registers for the union period may be held as a single set under Billy or may have been split across successors — PRONI's Guide to Church Records PDF (see Repository Guide below) is the definitive source on where each register now sits.
- In the Catholic ecclesiastical structure, the parish forms part of the district of Coleraine. Coleraine-district Catholic registers may therefore cover residents of Billy Civil Parish, and searching Coleraine records is necessary alongside any specifically-Billy Catholic registers.
- After 1922, County Antrim fell within Northern Ireland. All pre-1922 civil records for Antrim are held at PRONI (Belfast); the National Archives of Ireland (Dublin) holds parallel copies of some national records up to 1922 (civil registration, census, etc.). (Source: [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Civil registration of all births, marriages, and deaths began in Ireland on 1 January 1864 at the state level. Non-Catholic marriages were registerable from 1 April 1845. (Source: [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)) The FamilySearch Wiki pages for Ireland Civil Registration and Ireland Vital Records could not be loaded by the wiki tool during this survey; for exact registration district details, consult PRONI or the General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI).
- **What exists for 1780–1870:** Civil registration covers only the final six years of the target window (1864–1870). The great majority of this period — 1780–1863 — has no civil registration at all. Church registers are therefore the primary and often only source for vital events across nearly the entire target period.
- **Where held:** Births, marriages, and deaths registered from 1864 in Northern Ireland are held by the General Register Office Northern Ireland (GRONI), Oxford House, 49–55 Chichester Street, Belfast BT1 4HL; Tel: 028 9025 2000; Website: https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/contacts/contacts-az/general-register-office-northern-ireland. Indexes for Northern Ireland civil registration records are searchable on the GRONI website. The National Archives of Ireland in Dublin holds a parallel set of indexes for the island-wide registration period.

### Church records — PRIMARY SOURCE for 1780–1863

**Coverage gap in the FamilySearch Wiki:** The Billy Civil Parish FamilySearch Wiki page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy) lists the following sub-sections for church records — Catholic, Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, Methodist, Society of Friends, Others — but none of these sub-sections contain any content. No register start dates, no PRONI microfilm numbers, and no FamilySearch collection IDs are listed for any denomination in Billy parish. The wiki page directs researchers to the general [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records) article for further guidance. All repository and online-index recommendations in this section are drawn from that general article.

#### Church of Ireland
- Church of Ireland kept baptism, marriage, and burial registers from 1536, but approximately two-thirds of all pre-1922 Church of Ireland registers were destroyed in the fire at the Public Record Office in Dublin in 1922. (Source: [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)) Which Billy or union-parish registers survived is not stated in any tool result returned during this survey.
- Billy Civil Parish was formerly the head of a Church of Ireland ecclesiastical union comprising Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride. Surviving registers for the union period may be catalogued under Billy or one of the other parishes; the PRONI Guide to Church Records (PDF, see Repository Guide) will identify the exact title, date range, PRONI reference, and microfilm number for each set.
- Surviving registers are held at PRONI (Belfast) or, in some cases, at the Representative Church Body (RCB) Library in Dublin. The RCB Library's online search at https://store.ireland.anglican.org/genealogy and their downloadable Parish Registers list (https://www.ireland.anglican.org/cmsfiles/pdf/AboutUs/library/registers/ParishRegisters/PARISHREGISTERS.pdf) will show whether Billy's registers survived and where they are held.

#### Presbyterian (including Covenanters / Reformed Presbyterian)
- Billy Civil Parish had meeting houses for both Presbyterians and Covenanters (Reformed Presbyterians), confirmed by the FamilySearch Wiki. Presbyterian registers across Ireland average a start date of 1830, though some date to the 1600s. (Source: [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)) No specific start dates for Billy or Coleraine-area Presbyterian congregations were returned by any tool during this survey.
- The original registers are typically in the custody of the local congregation; PRONI holds microfilm copies of many Presbyterian registers for County Antrim. PRONI's Guide to Church Records PDF (https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf) will identify which Bushmills-area Presbyterian and Covenanting congregations have deposited records at PRONI and what microfilm numbers apply.
- Digitized Presbyterian and non-conformist records are searchable via FindMyPast's Ireland, Non-Conformist Births & Baptisms (https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-births-and-baptisms), Non-Conformist Marriages (https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-marriages), and Non-Conformist Burials (https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-burials) collections (subscription required). The Ulster Historical Foundation (https://www.ancestryireland.com/) and RootsIreland (https://www.rootsireland.ie/) also hold indexed Presbyterian records for County Antrim.

#### Catholic
- In the Catholic ecclesiastical structure, Billy Civil Parish forms part of the district of Coleraine; Catholic residents of Billy parish used Coleraine-district churches and their records fall within those registers, not a specifically-Billy parish register series.
- Most rural Catholic parishes in Ireland did not begin keeping registers until after Catholic Emancipation in 1828; some city parishes date to the 1750s. (Source: [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)) Catholic registers for the Coleraine district will therefore have little or no coverage for the first half of the target window (1780–1828).
- The National Library of Ireland (NLI) has digitized Catholic parish registers covering much of Ireland at no charge: https://registers.nli.ie/. Ancestry hosts Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1655–1915 (collection/61039, subscription) which indexes and images many of the same registers. The National Archives of Ireland website (https://www.nationalarchives.ie/article/records-birth-marriage-death/) also provides guidance on finding Catholic records.

#### Wesleyan Methodist
- The FamilySearch Wiki confirms a Wesleyan Methodist meeting house in Billy parish. Methodist record-keeping in Ireland began after the founding of the first Dublin society in 1746; Antrim-area registers are variable in start date.
- FindMyPast holds indexed non-conformist/Methodist records under Ireland, Non-Conformist Congregational Records (https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/ireland-non-conformist-congregational-records) (subscription required).

### Census records
- The tools were unable to load the FamilySearch Ireland Census wiki page during this survey. The following is therefore based solely on the general information returned by the Ireland Church Records page and cannot be verified against an Ireland-specific tool result: the 1901 and 1911 census returns for Ireland survive and are searchable free at https://census.nationalarchives.ie/; most pre-1901 census returns were destroyed (1821, 1831, 1841, and 1851 returns for County Antrim are substantially lost). The Griffith's Valuation (1847–1864) and the Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837) serve as census substitutes for the target period — but these facts come from general knowledge, not from a tool result returned during this survey. Consult https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Census and PRONI directly for verified coverage details.

### Probate and court records
- The tools could not load the Ireland Probate Records wiki page. Probate for the established church (Church of Ireland) fell under the Diocesan Consistorial Court and the Prerogative Court of Armagh until 1858, when a civil Probate Court took over.
- FamilySearch holds a free, indexed collection: Ireland, Diocesan and Prerogative Marriage License Bonds Indexes, 1623–1866 (collection/3460239, https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/3460239); also an Index to Prerogative Marriage License Bonds, ca. 1750–1849 (catalog/117060). These cover wills and administration bonds, not just marriages, and are useful substitutes for lost probate records. (Source: [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))
- Ancestry hosts Ireland, Indexes to Wills, Probate Administration, Marriage Bonds and Licences, 1591–1866 (collection/62077, subscription). PRONI holds probate records for Northern Ireland from 1858 onward and is the primary repository for post-1858 Antrim probate material.

### Land records
- The tools could not load the Ireland Land and Property wiki page. Land records for County Antrim include Crown and Quit Rent Office surveys, estate papers at PRONI, the Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837), and the Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864). These are standard census substitutes for the target period. PRONI holds extensive estate papers for the North Antrim and Coleraine area.
- The land distribution jurisdiction for Ireland in this period was the Crown (via the Board of Works and Quit Rent Office) and private landlords. Estate records (leases, rent rolls, maps) are held at PRONI for the Northern Ireland counties and at the National Archives of Ireland for the Republic.
- The FamilySearch Wiki Ireland Land and Property page could not be loaded; consult https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Land_and_Property directly.

### Military records
- Relevant conflicts include the 1798 United Irishmen rebellion, the Napoleonic Wars (1803–1815), and various British garrison activities throughout the period.
- British Army service records and pension files for Irish soldiers are held at The National Archives (UK), Kew, London, TW9 4DU; https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/. PRONI holds some militia muster rolls and yeomanry records for County Antrim.
- The tools could not load the Ireland Military Records wiki page; consult https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Military_Records for further guidance.

### Cemetery records
- The Billy Civil Parish wiki page does not list major cemeteries or sexton records for the parish. Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, and Catholic congregations each maintained burial grounds; burial registers (where they survive) are held at PRONI or the local congregation.
- FindAGrave (https://www.findagrave.com/) and BillionGraves (https://billiongraves.com/) both index some Northern Ireland graveyards, though rural County Antrim coverage is variable. The North Antrim heritage societies and Causeway Coast and Glens Borough Council may hold unpublished graveyard surveys for the Bushmills area.

### Newspaper records
- The Coleraine Chronicle (founded 1844) and the Belfast News-Letter (founded 1737, one of the longest-running English-language newspapers in the world) are the key papers covering the Billy parish area during the target window. Both carry obituaries, marriage notices, legal notices, and estate sale advertisements.
- The Belfast News-Letter is digitized and searchable at https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/ (subscription) and partially on FindMyPast (subscription). The Coleraine Chronicle has partial coverage at the same platforms and on microfilm at Coleraine Library.
- The British Newspaper Archive at https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/ is the primary online index for Northern Ireland papers of this period.

### Immigration and emigration records
- The Billy parish area experienced significant emigration during the Ulster emigration waves of the 1780s–1800s and again during and after the Great Famine (1845–1852). Emigrants typically left through Londonderry/Derry, Belfast, or Liverpool.
- Passenger lists for North American voyages are held at Library and Archives Canada (https://www.bac-lac.gc.ca/) and NARA (USA). The Famine-era Assisted Emigration records are held at PRONI.
- The FamilySearch collection Ireland, Emigration and Immigration records can be located via https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Emigration_and_Immigration. The Ulster Historical Foundation (https://www.ancestryireland.com/) and PRONI hold significant Antrim emigration documentation.
- Naturalization declarations for emigrants who settled in the United States, Canada, or Australia were generated in those countries. For emigrants to the United States, pre-1906 naturalizations can appear in any US court of record and are searchable via Ancestry and FamilySearch.

### Tax records
- The Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837) list landholders in each townland liable for tithe payments; they function as a census substitute for the mid-period target window. FamilySearch has an indexed collection of these (Ireland, Tithe Applotment Books, 1823–1837).
- The Griffith's Primary Valuation (1847–1864) lists every householder in Ireland and is the primary mid-century substitute for census records. It is searchable free at https://www.askaboutireland.ie/griffith-valuation/ and at https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/.
- These facts about Tithe Applotment and Griffith's Valuation come from general knowledge, not from a tool result returned during this survey; verify at PRONI or via the FamilySearch Ireland Taxation page (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Taxation).

## Records NOT online

- **Church of Ireland registers for Billy parish (and the former ecclesiastical union):** The FamilySearch Wiki church records section for Billy Civil Parish has no content — no register dates and no online collection IDs are listed. Whether the registers survived the 1922 fire and whether they are digitized is unconfirmed by any tool result. PRONI and the RCB Library must be consulted directly.
- **Presbyterian and Covenanting congregation registers for Billy/Bushmills area:** No specific congregation is named and no PRONI film number is listed for Billy parish on the FamilySearch Wiki. The PRONI Guide to Church Records PDF is the essential finding aid.
- **Catholic registers for the Coleraine district prior to 1828:** Most rural Catholic parishes in Ireland had not begun keeping records before Catholic Emancipation. The National Library of Ireland at registers.nli.ie is the starting point, but coverage before 1828 is likely sparse or absent.
- **Wesleyan Methodist congregation registers for Billy parish:** No collection details are listed for Billy in any tool result. FindMyPast's non-conformist collections and PRONI's Guide are the starting points.
- **Pre-1864 civil registration:** No civil registration exists for births, marriages, or deaths in Ireland before 1864.
- **Pre-1901 census returns for County Antrim:** Substantially destroyed (see Census section above). Griffith's Valuation and Tithe Applotment Books are the main substitutes.

---

## Known record losses

- The 1922 fire at the Public Record Office in Dublin destroyed approximately two-thirds of all Church of Ireland parish registers, along with large volumes of Irish historical records including many pre-1922 wills and census returns. (Source: [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records)) Whether Billy Civil Parish's Church of Ireland registers are among the surviving third is not stated in any tool result returned during this survey.
- No tool result returned during this survey states that Billy parish's specific registers — Presbyterian, Catholic, Methodist, or Church of Ireland — were lost. Absence of information is not confirmation of loss. PRONI and the repositories above must be consulted to determine which registers survive.
- The Betham, Crossle, and Thrift Genealogical Abstracts (available on FindMyPast) were compiled from pre-fire records and serve as partial substitutes for wills and other documents lost in 1922. (Source: [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))

---

## Research tips

- **Start with PRONI's Guide to Church Records.** Download the PDF at https://www.nidirect.gov.uk/sites/default/files/publications/Guide-to-Church-Records-October-2019.pdf and look up Billy parish (and the five parishes of the former ecclesiastical union: Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, Kilbride) for every denomination. This guide names exactly which registers survive, their date ranges, their PRONI MIC reference numbers, and whether they are digitized.
- **Search the former ecclesiastical union parishes alongside Billy itself.** Because Billy was formerly the head of a Church of Ireland union comprising Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride, registers covering families in Billy may be catalogued under any of those parishes, not just Billy. Treat all five as one continuous research trail for Church of Ireland records. (Source: [Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy))
- **For Catholic families, search the Coleraine district, not a Billy-specific register.** The Billy Civil Parish wiki page states that "In the Roman Catholic divisions the parish forms part of the district of Coleraine." (Source: [Billy Civil Parish, County Antrim, Northern Ireland Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Billy_Civil_Parish,_County_Antrim,_Northern_Ireland_Genealogy)) Search registers.nli.ie and Ancestry's collection/61039 under Coleraine, not under Billy.
- **Search Church of Ireland registers even if the family was not Church of Ireland.** Some families of other denominations used Church of Ireland rites for record-keeping purposes; some early registers are mixed. (Source: [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))
- **Use Griffith's Valuation (1847–1864) and the Tithe Applotment Books (1823–1837) as the census substitutes for the mid-period.** These cover virtually every household in the townlands of Billy parish and are the primary tools for locating families between the 1780s and the 1901 census.
- **Note gaps in church registers and search alternative record types.** The Ireland Church Records wiki advises: "Note gaps or missing pages in the record. You may want to search alternative records for the missing time periods... If you find little or no mention of your family in parish records, search other records." Estate papers at PRONI (which name tenants by name and townland), landed estate court records, and poorlaw union records may supply details for years where church registers are missing or were lost. (Source: [Ireland Church Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Ireland_Church_Records))

---

**Tool limitations affecting this guide:** The FamilySearch place_search, collections_search, volume_search, and external_links_search tools returned zero results for all Irish place queries — the tool infrastructure does not resolve Irish or Northern Irish place names to internal IDs. All four wiki_place_page sections (home, getting_started, online_records, research_tips) returned a generic fallback page rather than Northern Ireland-specific content. The wiki_read tool successfully loaded the Ireland Church Records page but returned the same generic "Genealogy Records" page for all other Ireland-specific URLs attempted (Ireland Civil Registration, Ireland Census, Ireland Land and Property, Ireland Probate Records, Ireland Presbyterian Church Records, Church of Ireland Records, Billy Civil Parish full page). The guide's record-type sections other than church records and civil registration therefore draw on the Ireland Church Records wiki page and the Billy Civil Parish wiki_search result only. Re-run this survey against those specific wiki pages (via the FamilySearch Wiki directly) before making decisions that depend on the detail in those sections.

---

Billy Civil Parish is a small rural parish in the North Antrim barony of Lower Dunluce, centered on the town of Bushmills. Across the 1780–1870 window the most important surviving records are church registers — but the FamilySearch Wiki page for the parish lists all denominations (Church of Ireland, Presbyterian, Covenanter, Methodist, Catholic) with no detail at all, so the first task before any other searching is to consult PRONI in Belfast, which holds microfilm copies of most County Antrim church registers, and to download their free Guide to Church Records PDF to find which specific Billy-area registers survive and where they are held. Civil registration of births and deaths only began in 1864, covering just the last six years of the target window, so church registers and land substitutes such as Griffith's Valuation and the Tithe Applotment Books carry the bulk of the evidence for the period.

The next step is to work through the PRONI Guide to Church Records for each denomination and each of the five parishes of Billy's former ecclesiastical union (Armoy, Ballyclug, Donegore, and Kilbride alongside Billy itself), then search the National Library of Ireland's free Catholic register images at registers.nli.ie for the Coleraine district, and run the Ulster Historical Foundation and RootsIreland indexes for County Antrim — after which a research plan can be drafted around the registers that actually survive.

dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.rationale: The guide is substantially accurate but contains a critical URL fidelity failure. The per-test context explicitly states that 'A repository URL the guide prints must be one the tools returned' and that 'Printing a URL no tool returned (e.g. ulsterancestry.com) is the first failure under test.' The guide lists 'Ulster Historical Foundation (https://www.ancestryireland.com/)' in the Repository Guide table. The tool result (Ireland Church Records wiki page) returned 'https://www.ancestryireland.com/' as the correct URL. However, the guide also states in the Presbyterian section: 'The Ulster Historical Foundation (https://www.ancestryireland.com/) and RootsIreland (https://www.rootsireland.ie/) also hold indexed Presbyterian records for County Antrim.' This is correct. But critically, the guide does not cite any tool result that returned 'ulsterancestry.com' — and the per-test context warns against printing URLs no tool returned. The guide's other factual claims about church records, civil registration dates (1864), the 1922 fire destroying two-thirds of Church of Ireland registers, the ecclesiastical union structure, and the Coleraine district Catholic jurisdiction are all supported by the wiki_search results. The guide correctly identifies that the Billy Civil Parish FamilySearch Wiki page has empty church records sections, which is confirmed by the wiki_search result showing the empty subsections. The guide appropriately flags this gap and directs researchers to PRONI and other repositories. However, the URL fidelity issue and the failure to connect some returned indexes to stated gaps (see Completeness) constitute factual/attribution errors.

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.rationale: The guide addresses most required elements but has a critical gap-connection failure flagged by the per-test context. The context states: 'When the guide states a record-availability gap and a tool result names an index/repository that bears on it, the guide should connect them rather than listing the repository as a generic fee-based service. Failing to connect a returned index to the stated gap is the second failure under test.' The guide identifies the gap in church records for Billy parish (the empty FamilySearch Wiki sections) and recommends PRONI, the National Library of Ireland, and various online repositories. However, when discussing Presbyterian records, the guide states 'No specific start dates for Billy or Coleraine-area Presbyterian congregations were returned by any tool during this survey' but then lists FindMyPast's non-conformist collections without explicitly connecting them to filling this gap. Similarly, for Catholic records, the guide notes 'Most rural Catholic parishes in Ireland did not begin keeping registers until after Catholic Emancipation in 1828' and identifies a coverage gap for 1780–1828, then recommends the National Library of Ireland and Ancestry — but does not explicitly state that these repositories address the pre-1828 gap. The guide does provide comprehensive coverage of vital records, census records, probate, land records, military records, cemetery records, newspaper records, emigration records, and tax records. It includes two detailed repository tables with addresses and URLs. The research tips section is thorough. However, the failure to explicitly connect returned indexes to the stated gaps (as required by the per-test context) is a concrete omission of the required connection work.

# Locality Guide: Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania (1840–1869)

## Jurisdiction Overview

Schuylkill County was formed in 1811 from Berks and Northampton counties. It has had stable boundaries since formation — events before 1811 will be found under those predecessor counties. No statewide civil vital-records registration existed during the 1840s–1860s, making church registers the primary source for births and deaths.

---

## Available Record Types

### Vital Records (Civil Registration)
- **Status:** No civil registration for this period was confirmed. Pennsylvania did not have statewide vital-records registration in the 1840s–1860s.
- **Substitutes:** Church baptism, marriage, and burial registers; federal census (1850, 1860) for approximate birth years and family relationships.

### Church Records
- **Denominations confirmed:** Lutheran (others not confirmed by available tools).
- **Digitized volume:** Lutheran Church Records, 1840–1875 — **browse-only, partly in German.** No name index; no full-text search. Must be searched image by image.
- **Where held:** FamilySearch holds digitized images; originals at the parish or denominational archives.

### Census Records
- **Most accessible source:** U.S. Federal Census, 1850–1860 — **96% name-indexed and full-text searchable** on FamilySearch. This is the best starting point for any person search in the county.
- **Ancestry:** Also hosts the 1850 federal census for Schuylkill County (subscription required).
- **1840 census:** Not confirmed as a digitized FamilySearch volume — check Ancestry.
- **Mortality schedules (1850, 1860):** Not confirmed as a separate digitized volume; worth locating for death information in the absence of death registration.

### Probate Records
- **FamilySearch Collection:** "Pennsylvania, Probate Records, 1683–1994" — 3.2 million images, **browse-only** (zero name-indexed records).
- **Digitized volume:** Probate Records, 1845–1880 — only 4% name-indexed; full-text search available for the rest. Expect to browse images.
- **Record types:** Wills, administrations, inventories, guardianships.
- **Where held:** County courthouse (Schuylkill County Register of Wills); FamilySearch holds digitized images.

### Land Records
- **Online status:** No digitized land records for 1840–1869 were found. Pennsylvania is a metes-and-bounds state.
- **Where held:** Deed books at the county Recorder of Deeds; warrant/survey records at the Pennsylvania State Archives.

### Military Records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Mexican-American War (1846–1848), Civil War (1861–1865).
- **Online status:** No Schuylkill County–specific military volume was found for this period.
- **Where held:** Service records and pension files at NARA; state militia/adjutant general records at Pennsylvania State Archives. Pre-1906 pension files are especially valuable for establishing birth dates, relationships, and place of origin.

### Cemetery Records
- **Online status:** No digitized cemetery collection confirmed for this county and period.
- **Where to look:** FindAGrave, BillionGraves; Schuylkill County Historical Society may hold transcribed burial records.

### Newspapers
- **Online status:** No digitized newspaper collection confirmed for this period. The *Miners' Journal* (Pottsville) was published during this era — microfilm may be available at Pennsylvania libraries.

### Immigration / Naturalization Records
- **Port:** Philadelphia is the nearest major port of entry.
- **Naturalization:** Before 1906, any court of record could grant citizenship — search county, state, and federal district court records as separate series.

### Tax Records
- **Online status:** No county-level tax records for 1840–1869 confirmed. The only returned Ancestry tax collection (1768–1801) predates this period by nearly 40 years.
- **Where held:** County courthouse.

---

## Repository Guide

### Online
| Repository | Holdings | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Federal Census 1850–1860 (96% indexed); Probate Records 1845–1880 (4% indexed, full-text); Lutheran Church Records 1840–1875 (browse-only) | Free |
| Ancestry | 1850 Federal Census — Schuylkill County | Subscription |

### Physical
| Repository | Holdings |
|---|---|
| Schuylkill County Courthouse | Deed books, probate originals, court minutes, naturalizations |
| Pennsylvania State Archives (Harrisburg) | Warrant/survey files, state militia/adjutant general records |
| Schuylkill County Historical Society | County histories, newspaper transcriptions, cemetery records |
| Denominational archives | Lutheran and other church register originals |
| NARA (Philadelphia) | Civil War service and pension records, pre-1906 naturalizations |

---

## Records NOT Online

The following must be accessed through physical repositories or microfilm:
- Land/deed records (1840–1869)
- Tax records (1840–1869)
- Military records specific to Schuylkill County
- Cemetery and sexton records
- Newspapers
- Mortality schedules (1850, 1860) — not confirmed as a separate digitized volume
- 1840 federal census — not on FamilySearch

---

## Key Research Tips

1. **Church records are the vital-record substitute for this entire period.** No civil registration start date was confirmed for Pennsylvania in the 1840s–1860s. Lutheran registers (1840–1875) are digitized but browse-only and partly in German — allow extra time and language preparation.

2. **Start with the 1850 and 1860 federal censuses.** At 96% indexed and full-text searchable, they are the most accessible starting point for any person search.

3. **Probate records are mostly browse-only.** Only 4% of the 1845–1880 volume is name-indexed. Try full-text search first, then plan to browse images.

4. **Naturalization records may be scattered across multiple courts.** Search county, state, and federal courts as separate series.

5. **A negative online result is not an absence.** Many Schuylkill County records for this period are either not digitized or held only in physical repositories. An online nil-result does not mean the record doesn't exist.

6. **Identify the specific township or borough** of interest to target the right church register volume and narrow courthouse searches.

entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Pulaski County, Kentucky (1840–1880)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** 1798 from Lincoln and Green counties
- **County seat / administrative center:** Not confirmed from tool results in this survey
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Kentucky (state since 1792; prior to 1792 the territory was part of Virginia)
- **Population during period:** No population data was returned by the place_population tool for Pulaski County during this period
- **Economy:** Not stated by any tool result for this county specifically
- **Ethnic composition:** Not stated by any tool result for this county specifically
- **Religious denominations:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian were the largest groups in Kentucky before 1900 (Kentucky Church Records wiki)
- **Key historical events:** Civil War (1861–1865) — Kentucky was a border state with residents serving on both Union and Confederate sides

## Boundary changes
- Pulaski County was formed in 1798 from Lincoln and Green counties; events occurring before 1798 are recorded in those two parent jurisdictions.
- place_search_all returned only one representation for Pulaski County, with date range from 1798 forward — no subsequent boundary changes are recorded in that tool result.

## Available record types

All record types are held at the **county level** unless otherwise noted.

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start dates:**
  - County-level births and deaths: intermittent — 1853–1862, 1874–1878, and 1892–1910; compliance was poor throughout all three periods
  - County-level marriages: continuous from county formation (1798)
  - Statewide births and deaths: began 1911; general compliance by 1917
  - Statewide marriage registration: 1958
- **What exists for 1840–1880:** Marriage records (county level) exist for the entire period; birth and death records exist only for 1853–1862 and 1874–1878, and even those have significant gaps due to poor compliance
- **Where held:** Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), Frankfort, for pre-1911 county records; Pulaski County courthouse for marriage bonds and licenses; Kentucky Department of Public Health, Office of Vital Statistics, for records from 1911 onward
- **Gaps:** No civil birth or death records for 1840–1853, 1862–1874, or 1878–1892
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church baptism, marriage, and burial records (see Church records below)
- **Source:** https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian — the largest groups in Kentucky before 1900
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations, membership lists, church minutes
- **Where held:** FamilySearch Library (microfilm); Kentucky Historical Society (Frankfort, manuscripts); Filson Historical Society (Louisville, Baptist/Methodist/Presbyterian for the broader region); individual denominational archives (Southern Baptist Historical Library, Nashville; Presbyterian Historical Society, Philadelphia; various Methodist conference archives); active congregations may hold their own records
- **FamilySearch collections (from Kentucky Church Records wiki):**
  - Kentucky Church Records 1818–1995: index and images (incomplete)
  - Kentucky Births and Christenings 1839–1960: index only
  - Kentucky Marriages 1785–1979: index only
  - Kentucky Deaths and Burials 1843–1970: index only
- **Language:** English
- **Catholic diocese:** Pulaski County falls within one of four Kentucky Catholic dioceses (Covington, Lexington, Louisville, or Owensboro); the specific county assignment was not confirmed by tool results — consult the FamilySearch Wiki's diocese county tables
- **Source:** https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records

### Census records
- **Federal census:** Kentucky counties were enumerated from 1810; for 1840–1880, the federal enumerations are 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880. Mortality schedules (deaths in the preceding year) were taken alongside the 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 censuses.
- **State census:** No Kentucky state censuses were taken (Kentucky Genealogy wiki)
- **Other enumerations:** None confirmed by tool results for this county
- **Access:** Federal censuses are indexed on FamilySearch and Ancestry; however, FamilySearch collections_search and volume_search did not resolve Pulaski County records during this survey (see Coverage note in Repository guide)
- **Source:** https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky,_United_States_Genealogy

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, estate administrations, guardianships, inventories; also naturalizations (pre-1906), name changes, civil and criminal cases at the county courthouse
- **Date range:** From county formation (1798); for the target period, the full 1840–1880 range should have records
- **Where held:** Pulaski County courthouse; KDLA (Frankfort) holds microfilmed county records
- **Digitized coverage:** Not confirmed — catalog_search returned 0 results at both county and Kentucky state levels (a cataloguing gap; does not mean records do not exist)

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (Kentucky is a state-land state)
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Virginia Land Office issued grants before 1792; Kentucky Land Office (Frankfort) issued grants from 1793 onward; county courthouses hold deed books from formation
- **Grant periods covering 1840–1880:** Old Kentucky Grants (1793–1856); Kentucky Land Warrants (1816–1873); County Court Orders (1836–1955)
- **Types:** Deeds (county courthouse from 1798), grants, patents, warrants, surveys; county deed books may reveal wives' given names, previous residences, and children's names
- **Where held:** Pulaski County courthouse (deed books); Kentucky Land Office, Frankfort (grants, warrants, surveys, patents); Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort
- **Online:** FamilySearch — Kentucky Land Office warrants, surveys, grants and related records (1700–1955), digitized images; Ancestry — Kentucky land grants
- **Source:** https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Mexican-American War (1846–1848); Civil War (1861–1865); as a border state, Kentucky residents served on both Union and Confederate sides
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files, bounty land warrants (all at NARA); Kentucky state adjutant general records at KDLA
- **Where held:** NARA (Washington DC / College Park); KDLA (Frankfort) for state records
- **Online:** Fold3 (subscription) for federal military records; NARA online for some Civil War pension index

### Cemetery records
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (findagrave.com) is available as a general resource; specific Pulaski County coverage not confirmed from tool results
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and burial registers at individual cemeteries or churches; county genealogical societies may hold survey transcriptions

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Specific Pulaski County newspaper titles were not returned by any tool in this survey
- **Where held:** Kentucky Historical Society (Frankfort); University of Kentucky Special Collections (Lexington); Newspapers.com (subscription)
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, estate/legal notices

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Pulaski County is inland in south-central Kentucky; no land borders or ports of entry are nearby. Declarations of intention, naturalizations, and alien registrations were nonetheless generated locally.
- **Record types:** Pre-1906 naturalizations at county and circuit courts; NARA for post-1906 federal naturalization records
- **Where held:** Pulaski County courthouse and KDLA for pre-1906 naturalizations; NARA for federal records
- **Content note:** Passenger arrival manifests were filed at ports of entry. For inland Pulaski County residents the relevant inland records are naturalization petitions and declarations of intention — search those at the county courthouse and KDLA.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Property tax lists, personal property; Kentucky counties produced annual tax lists
- **Date range:** From county formation (1798); annual coverage through the 1840–1880 period
- **Where held:** Pulaski County courthouse; KDLA; Kentucky Historical Society
- **Substitute value:** Kentucky tax lists are the most reliable intercensal substitute — they name taxable males each year and can track a family's presence or departure. Especially valuable between federal census years and as a replacement for the largely destroyed 1890 federal census.

### Other record types
- **County court minute books:** Record county road assignments, payments to indigent residents, local contracts — name people who never appear in probate or civil suits
- **Town and county histories:** 19th–early 20th century Kentucky county histories frequently reprint early records and are sometimes the only surviving transcription of since-lost originals

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch (familysearch.org) | Kentucky Church Records 1818–1995 (index + images, incomplete); Kentucky Births and Christenings 1839–1960 (index); Kentucky Marriages 1785–1979 (index); Kentucky Deaths and Burials 1843–1970 (index); Kentucky Land Office records 1700–1955 (images); see coverage note below | Free |
| Ancestry (ancestry.com) | U.S. Federal Census Collection; Kentucky land grants | Subscription |
| FindAGrave (findagrave.com) | Cemetery records | Free |
| Newspapers.com | Historical newspapers | Subscription |
| Fold3 (fold3.com) | Military service and pension records | Subscription |
| NARA (archives.gov) | Federal census, military service, pension, naturalization | Free (online index) / fee-based copies |

**Coverage of this survey:** FamilySearch's collections_search and volume_search tools did not resolve Pulaski County during this survey run (the standardPlace field returned empty in both tools' query output, and both returned 0 results). The FamilySearch catalog likewise returned 0 results at both county and Kentucky state levels. The collection names cited above come from directly fetched wiki pages (Kentucky Church Records, Kentucky Land and Property), not from a live collections query. The actual breadth of FamilySearch's Pulaski County digitized holdings is unconfirmed — search FamilySearch directly to determine current coverage before treating these gaps as definitive.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Pulaski County Courthouse, Somerset, KY | Marriage bonds/licenses (from 1798), deed books, probate files, court records | In-person; write to County Clerk |
| Kentucky Dept. for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), Frankfort | Pre-1911 county birth/death records (intermittent); microfilmed county records | In-person; online catalog at kdla.ky.gov |
| Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort | Manuscripts, newspapers, genealogical collections, land records | In-person; online catalog |
| Kentucky Land Office, Frankfort | Land grants, warrants, surveys, patents from 1793 | In-person; some digitized at FamilySearch |
| University of Kentucky Special Collections, Lexington | Newspapers, manuscripts | In-person |
| FamilySearch Library, Salt Lake City | Microfilmed church and county records | In-person; some via interlibrary loan |

## Records NOT online
- Pre-1911 Pulaski County civil birth and death records (even those from the 1853–1862 and 1874–1878 registration periods) — held at KDLA; digitized availability not confirmed
- County courthouse probate, court, and deed records — not confirmed as digitized by any tool result
- Individual church registers for specific Pulaski County congregations — most held by the congregation or denomination; not all are digitized
- Pre-1906 naturalization records at the county courthouse

## Known record losses
No tool result in this survey states that specific Pulaski County record sets were destroyed or lost. An absence from the FamilySearch catalog is a cataloguing gap, not a confirmed loss. Contact the Pulaski County Courthouse and KDLA directly to determine what survives for specific record types and date ranges.

## Research tips
- Kentucky civil birth and death registration was intermittent and poorly observed from 1853 to 1910. For 1840–1880 specifically, church records are the primary source for vital events — do not assume a civil birth or death record exists for any given year. (Kentucky Vital Records: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)
- Kentucky marriage records run continuously from county formation (1798) at the county level — these are the most consistently held vital record for the target period, held at the Pulaski County courthouse and KDLA. (Kentucky Vital Records: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)
- Kentucky has no state census. Between federal census years, use annual county tax lists as the primary substitute — they list taxable males each year and can confirm a family's presence in the county year by year. (Kentucky, United States Genealogy: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky,_United_States_Genealogy)
- Kentucky is a state-land state; land grants came from the Virginia Land Office before 1792 and the Kentucky Land Office thereafter. For the 1840–1880 period, search both county deed books (at the courthouse) and the Kentucky Land Office records (some digitized on FamilySearch). (Kentucky Land and Property: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property)
- For Civil War research (1861–1865), Kentucky's border-state status means residents served on both sides. Search Union service records (NARA, Fold3) and Confederate pension records (KDLA held Kentucky Confederate pensions), not just one side.
- Pulaski County formed from Lincoln and Green counties in 1798. For families researched before that date, or for pre-formation land grants, search both Lincoln and Green county records.

- Pulaski County was formed in 1798 from Lincoln and Green counties; events occurring before 1798 are recorded in those two parent jurisdictions.
- place_search_all returned only one representation for Pulaski County, with date range from 1798 forward — no subsequent boundary changes are recorded in that tool result.

## Available record types

All record types are held at the **county level** unless otherwise noted.

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start dates:**
  - County-level births and deaths: intermittent — 1853–1862, 1874–1878, and 1892–1910; compliance was poor throughout all three periods
  - County-level marriages: continuous from county formation (1798)
  - Statewide births and deaths: began 1911; general compliance by 1917
  - Statewide marriage registration: 1958
- **What exists for 1840–1880:** Marriage records (county level) exist for the entire period; birth and death records exist only for 1853–1862 and 1874–1878, and even those have significant gaps due to poor compliance
- **Where held:** Kentucky Department for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), Frankfort, for pre-1911 county records; Pulaski County courthouse for marriage bonds and licenses; Kentucky Department of Public Health, Office of Vital Statistics, for records from 1911 onward
- **Gaps:** No civil birth or death records for 1840–1853, 1862–1874, or 1878–1892
- **Pre-registration alternatives:** Church baptism, marriage, and burial records (see Church records below)
- **Source:** https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Baptist, Methodist, Roman Catholic, and Presbyterian — the largest groups in Kentucky before 1900
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, confirmations, membership lists, church minutes
- **Where held:** FamilySearch Library (microfilm); Kentucky Historical Society (Frankfort, manuscripts); Filson Historical Society (Louisville, Baptist/Methodist/Presbyterian for the broader region); individual denominational archives (Southern Baptist Historical Library, Nashville; Presbyterian Historical Society, Philadelphia; various Methodist conference archives); active congregations may hold their own records
- **FamilySearch collections (from Kentucky Church Records wiki):**
  - Kentucky Church Records 1818–1995: index and images (incomplete)
  - Kentucky Births and Christenings 1839–1960: index only
  - Kentucky Marriages 1785–1979: index only
  - Kentucky Deaths and Burials 1843–1970: index only
- **Language:** English
- **Catholic diocese:** Pulaski County falls within one of four Kentucky Catholic dioceses (Covington, Lexington, Louisville, or Owensboro); the specific county assignment was not confirmed by tool results — consult the FamilySearch Wiki's diocese county tables
- **Source:** https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Church_Records

### Census records
- **Federal census:** Kentucky counties were enumerated from 1810; for 1840–1880, the federal enumerations are 1840, 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880. Mortality schedules (deaths in the preceding year) were taken alongside the 1850, 1860, 1870, and 1880 censuses.
- **State census:** No Kentucky state censuses were taken (Kentucky Genealogy wiki)
- **Other enumerations:** None confirmed by tool results for this county
- **Access:** Federal censuses are indexed on FamilySearch and Ancestry; however, FamilySearch collections_search and volume_search did not resolve Pulaski County records during this survey (see Coverage note in Repository guide)
- **Source:** https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky,_United_States_Genealogy

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, estate administrations, guardianships, inventories; also naturalizations (pre-1906), name changes, civil and criminal cases at the county courthouse
- **Date range:** From county formation (1798); for the target period, the full 1840–1880 range should have records
- **Where held:** Pulaski County courthouse; KDLA (Frankfort) holds microfilmed county records
- **Digitized coverage:** Not confirmed — catalog_search returned 0 results at both county and Kentucky state levels (a cataloguing gap; does not mean records do not exist)

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (Kentucky is a state-land state)
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** Virginia Land Office issued grants before 1792; Kentucky Land Office (Frankfort) issued grants from 1793 onward; county courthouses hold deed books from formation
- **Grant periods covering 1840–1880:** Old Kentucky Grants (1793–1856); Kentucky Land Warrants (1816–1873); County Court Orders (1836–1955)
- **Types:** Deeds (county courthouse from 1798), grants, patents, warrants, surveys; county deed books may reveal wives' given names, previous residences, and children's names
- **Where held:** Pulaski County courthouse (deed books); Kentucky Land Office, Frankfort (grants, warrants, surveys, patents); Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort
- **Online:** FamilySearch — Kentucky Land Office warrants, surveys, grants and related records (1700–1955), digitized images; Ancestry — Kentucky land grants
- **Source:** https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Mexican-American War (1846–1848); Civil War (1861–1865); as a border state, Kentucky residents served on both Union and Confederate sides
- **Record types:** Service records, pension files, bounty land warrants (all at NARA); Kentucky state adjutant general records at KDLA
- **Where held:** NARA (Washington DC / College Park); KDLA (Frankfort) for state records
- **Online:** Fold3 (subscription) for federal military records; NARA online for some Civil War pension index

### Cemetery records
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave (findagrave.com) is available as a general resource; specific Pulaski County coverage not confirmed from tool results
- **Physical records:** Sexton records and burial registers at individual cemeteries or churches; county genealogical societies may hold survey transcriptions

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** Specific Pulaski County newspaper titles were not returned by any tool in this survey
- **Where held:** Kentucky Historical Society (Frankfort); University of Kentucky Special Collections (Lexington); Newspapers.com (subscription)
- **Content value:** Obituaries, marriage notices, estate/legal notices

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant ports:** Pulaski County is inland in south-central Kentucky; no land borders or ports of entry are nearby. Declarations of intention, naturalizations, and alien registrations were nonetheless generated locally.
- **Record types:** Pre-1906 naturalizations at county and circuit courts; NARA for post-1906 federal naturalization records
- **Where held:** Pulaski County courthouse and KDLA for pre-1906 naturalizations; NARA for federal records
- **Content note:** Passenger arrival manifests were filed at ports of entry. For inland Pulaski County residents the relevant inland records are naturalization petitions and declarations of intention — search those at the county courthouse and KDLA.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Property tax lists, personal property; Kentucky counties produced annual tax lists
- **Date range:** From county formation (1798); annual coverage through the 1840–1880 period
- **Where held:** Pulaski County courthouse; KDLA; Kentucky Historical Society
- **Substitute value:** Kentucky tax lists are the most reliable intercensal substitute — they name taxable males each year and can track a family's presence or departure. Especially valuable between federal census years and as a replacement for the largely destroyed 1890 federal census.

### Other record types
- **County court minute books:** Record county road assignments, payments to indigent residents, local contracts — name people who never appear in probate or civil suits
- **Town and county histories:** 19th–early 20th century Kentucky county histories frequently reprint early records and are sometimes the only surviving transcription of since-lost originals

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch (familysearch.org) | Kentucky Church Records 1818–1995 (index + images, incomplete); Kentucky Births and Christenings 1839–1960 (index); Kentucky Marriages 1785–1979 (index); Kentucky Deaths and Burials 1843–1970 (index); Kentucky Land Office records 1700–1955 (images); see coverage note below | Free |
| Ancestry (ancestry.com) | U.S. Federal Census Collection; Kentucky land grants | Subscription |
| FindAGrave (findagrave.com) | Cemetery records | Free |
| Newspapers.com | Historical newspapers | Subscription |
| Fold3 (fold3.com) | Military service and pension records | Subscription |
| NARA (archives.gov) | Federal census, military service, pension, naturalization | Free (online index) / fee-based copies |

**Coverage of this survey:** FamilySearch's collections_search and volume_search tools did not resolve Pulaski County during this survey run (the standardPlace field returned empty in both tools' query output, and both returned 0 results). The FamilySearch catalog likewise returned 0 results at both county and Kentucky state levels. The collection names cited above come from directly fetched wiki pages (Kentucky Church Records, Kentucky Land and Property), not from a live collections query. The actual breadth of FamilySearch's Pulaski County digitized holdings is unconfirmed — search FamilySearch directly to determine current coverage before treating these gaps as definitive.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Pulaski County Courthouse, Somerset, KY | Marriage bonds/licenses (from 1798), deed books, probate files, court records | In-person; write to County Clerk |
| Kentucky Dept. for Libraries and Archives (KDLA), Frankfort | Pre-1911 county birth/death records (intermittent); microfilmed county records | In-person; online catalog at kdla.ky.gov |
| Kentucky Historical Society, Frankfort | Manuscripts, newspapers, genealogical collections, land records | In-person; online catalog |
| Kentucky Land Office, Frankfort | Land grants, warrants, surveys, patents from 1793 | In-person; some digitized at FamilySearch |
| University of Kentucky Special Collections, Lexington | Newspapers, manuscripts | In-person |
| FamilySearch Library, Salt Lake City | Microfilmed church and county records | In-person; some via interlibrary loan |

## Records NOT online
- Pre-1911 Pulaski County civil birth and death records (even those from the 1853–1862 and 1874–1878 registration periods) — held at KDLA; digitized availability not confirmed
- County courthouse probate, court, and deed records — not confirmed as digitized by any tool result
- Individual church registers for specific Pulaski County congregations — most held by the congregation or denomination; not all are digitized
- Pre-1906 naturalization records at the county courthouse

## Known record losses
No tool result in this survey states that specific Pulaski County record sets were destroyed or lost. An absence from the FamilySearch catalog is a cataloguing gap, not a confirmed loss. Contact the Pulaski County Courthouse and KDLA directly to determine what survives for specific record types and date ranges.

## Research tips
- Kentucky civil birth and death registration was intermittent and poorly observed from 1853 to 1910. For 1840–1880 specifically, church records are the primary source for vital events — do not assume a civil birth or death record exists for any given year. (Kentucky Vital Records: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)
- Kentucky marriage records run continuously from county formation (1798) at the county level — these are the most consistently held vital record for the target period, held at the Pulaski County courthouse and KDLA. (Kentucky Vital Records: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Vital_Records)
- Kentucky has no state census. Between federal census years, use annual county tax lists as the primary substitute — they list taxable males each year and can confirm a family's presence in the county year by year. (Kentucky, United States Genealogy: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky,_United_States_Genealogy)
- Kentucky is a state-land state; land grants came from the Virginia Land Office before 1792 and the Kentucky Land Office thereafter. For the 1840–1880 period, search both county deed books (at the courthouse) and the Kentucky Land Office records (some digitized on FamilySearch). (Kentucky Land and Property: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Kentucky_Land_and_Property)
- For Civil War research (1861–1865), Kentucky's border-state status means residents served on both sides. Search Union service records (NARA, Fold3) and Confederate pension records (KDLA held Kentucky Confederate pensions), not just one side.
- Pulaski County formed from Lincoln and Green counties in 1798. For families researched before that date, or for pre-formation land grants, search both Lincoln and Green county records.

output.text_response:
Locality guide saved as **loc_001** in the project.

---

You are researching the Alabama region around 1800, a period when no state of Alabama existed yet. The territory was part of the **Mississippi Territory** from 1798 to 1817, and the **Mobile area** in the south had been under French, British, and Spanish colonial administration before the U.S. gained control in 1813. That split means your ancestor's records could sit in one of two completely different record trails depending on where in Alabama they lived.

**Key repositories for this period:**

- **Alabama Department of Archives and History** (Montgomery) — holds territorial censuses from 1801, 1805, and 1808, militia rolls, and deed records.
- **County probate courts** — marriage and probate records from each county's formation date; the earliest is Washington County, formed 1800.
- **National Archives** — military and naturalization records.
- **Spanish colonial archives** (Seville) and their copies at the **Library of Congress** — essential for the Mobile area, which was under Spanish control until 1813.

**FamilySearch collections available:**
- Marriages from 1809
- Probate records from 1809
- Church records from 1803
- Census substitutes from 1810
- Three digitized volumes of territorial court and land records (1803–1820) — browsable image-by-image, no name index

**Critical caution:** Always search under **"Mississippi Territory"** rather than "Alabama" on any genealogy platform, because that is the jurisdiction that created the records during most of this period.

**Next step:** Identify which specific county your ancestor likely lived in, then target that county's formation date and its surviving records directly.

quirks: Around 1800, the Alabama region was part of the Mississippi Territory (1798-1817). Many records from this period are filed under 'Mississippi Territory' or 'Mississippi,' not 'Alabama' — search both jurisdictions on FamilySearch and in physical archives.

The Mobile area (southern Alabama) has a completely separate colonial record trail: French (1702-1763), British (1763-1780), and Spanish (1780-1813). These records are held in European archives and their American copies, not at the Alabama Department of Archives and History.

Alabama is a federal land state. Pre-statehood land grants came from Spain, Britain, Georgia, and the U.S. government; search the BLM General Land Office (GLO) records portal for federal patents, and the ADAH and Library of Congress for colonial-era grants.

No statewide civil registration of births or deaths existed in this period. County marriage registers are the main civil vital record from the territorial era. The specific start dates per county depend on when each county was formed — Washington County (1800) is the earliest.

The territorial censuses of 1801, 1805, 1808, and 1810 for the Mississippi Territory (covering present-day Alabama) are held at the Alabama Department of Archives and History (ADAH) in Montgomery — these are distinct from the 1810 federal census.

The FamilySearch Wiki pages for Alabama Vital Records, Alabama Land and Property, and Alabama Church Records did not load specific content during this survey — redirected to a generic records overview. Re-run the locality guide or consult those pages directly before relying on their absence.

The four wiki_place_page sections (home, getting_started, online_records, research_tips) all returned a generic Genealogy Research Guide page rather than Alabama-specific content.
